explanations.1908-portuguese-legislative-election--re: The Chamber returned in April 1908 was the most fragmented the monarchy had produced: both parties of the rotation had split, no group held a majority, and the ministries drawn from it lasted months each. The claim here is deliberately narrow. The election did not cause the revolution, and no historian argues that it did; it produced the parliamentary deadlock the revolution happened inside, and against which republican propaganda that the regime could no longer govern itself was simply accurate.
explanations.1911-portuguese-constituent-national-ass: The Assembly elected on 28 May met in June as a constituent body and did the one thing it had been elected to do: it wrote the constitution and promulgated it on 21 August. The near-unanimity of the election is visible in the text — a parliamentary republic with a weak presidency, written by a party that had no opposition in the room and did not expect to acquire one.
explanations.1911-portuguese-presidential-election--p: What the Congress filled in August 1911 was an office with few powers but one large one: the president appointed and dismissed ministers. In January 1915 Arriaga used it against the Chamber, dismissing the Democratic government and calling General Pimenta de Castro, who governed with parliament suspended. The argument is about the office as much as the man — the 1911 settlement had left a constitutional route by which a president could set the parliamentary majority aside, and this is the first time it was walked.
explanations.1915-portuguese-legislative-election--ge: Intervention was Democratic policy and it was contested: much of the army, the Evolutionists in part, and most of the country outside Lisbon had no wish to be in the war. The majority returned in June 1915 is what made the policy executable — it was a Democratic government that requisitioned the seventy-odd German ships in Portuguese harbours in February 1916 at Britain’s request, and the German declaration followed a fortnight later. The claim is not that the election caused the declaration, but that the government which provoked it could not have been formed without the June result.
explanations.1921-portuguese-legislative-election--no: The men killed on the night of 19 October were the government and its friends, and this election is what made them the government. The Republican Liberals had assembled themselves to take the chamber from the Democrats and had succeeded in July; the column that went through Lisbon in October was made of the Democrats' own constituency in the armed forces and the arsenals, acting against a ministry it took to be restoring the men of the monarchy. The edge is `precondition-of` and not `caused`: what the election produced was the target, and what produced the killing was the politics of the barracks.
explanations.1925-portuguese-legislative-election--co: A coup needs something to overthrow, and what 28 May 1926 overthrew was this parliament and the government drawn from it. The edge claims no more than that and deliberately not the more interesting thing — that the ballot of November 1925 caused the coup — because the case against the Republic was made on fifteen years of instability rather than on this result. What makes the election worth a record is what the coup then did with it: the Chamber elected in 1925 was the last chosen from more than one list for half a century, and everything the atlas holds between here and 1975 is the working out of that.
explanations.1928-portuguese-presidential-election--s: This edge is deliberately narrower than the one the atlas already carries from the coup. What drove the dictatorship to Salazar’s terms was its own financial failure, and that argument is made there. What the March election added was the authority to concede them: the appointment of April 1928 was made by a government formed under a president confirmed a month earlier by a national vote, and the veto Salazar demanded bound every other ministry, which a junta improvising its own legitimacy was in no position to promise. The claim is about the terms and who could grant them, not about why he was wanted.
explanations.1945-portuguese-legislative-election--19: What 1945 taught the democratic opposition was that the regime would concede the form of a contest when it wanted something from abroad, and would concede nothing that decided one — not the rolls, not the censorship, not the count. The campaign for Norton de Matos was built on that reading. It went for the presidency rather than the Assembly, because a single national candidacy could not be taken apart constituency by constituency, and it went early and in the open. It ended the same way and for the same reasons, which is the point of putting the two side by side.
explanations.1945-portuguese-legislative-election--de: This edge is about organisation rather than about the idea. The MUD lasted three years and achieved nothing it set out to achieve, but for a few months it put republicans, socialists and communists into one working front, and the people who learned each other there are the people who supplied candidates, committees and lawyers to every opposition campaign that followed. A national candidacy mounted in weeks, as Delgado’s was in 1958, presupposes a network already in existence. That network was assembled in the autumn of 1945.
explanations.1948-arab-israeli-war--1952-egyptian-rev: The Free Officers were made in Palestine. The defeat of 1948, the scandal over defective weapons bought by the palace, and the conviction that the army had been sent to fight with nothing by a government that was corrupt and a king who was worse are what the officers who took power on 23 July 1952 said had brought them together; Nasser and Naguib had both served in that war. The claim is about the movement and its grievance. Egypt in 1952 had other causes as well, the British presence in the canal zone above all, and this edge does not claim to be the only one.
explanations.1948-arab-israeli-war--lebanese-civil-wa: The Palestinian refugee population in Lebanon is what the war of 1948 put there, and it is the standing term in every account of how the civil war began: by 1975 it numbered more than 300,000, and the PLO had made of southern Lebanon an unofficial state within a state, which the English article says then played an important role in the civil war. This is a precondition and not a cause. The confessional settlement of 1943, the Cairo agreement of 1969 and the arrival of the PLO leadership from Jordan after 1970 are each part of the same account, and none of them is a record here; what is claimed is that without the population the 1948 war displaced there is no Lebanese civil war of the shape that happened.
explanations.1948-arab-israeli-war--yom-kippur-war--p: This edge states its own gap. The wars of 1948, 1956, 1967 and 1973 are rounds of one conflict, and the atlas holds only the first and the last: the territory Egypt and Syria attacked to recover in October 1973 was taken in 1967, not in 1948, so the chain runs through two records that are not here. What survives the gap is the conflict itself, which 1948 began and which no settlement had ended, and the armistice lines of 1949 that every later round was fought over. Until 1956 and 1967 are records here this edge should be read as a placeholder for three, and it is marked probable for that reason as much as any other.
explanations.1948-czechoslovak-coup-d-etat--european-: The convention of 1950 was drafted as an alarm bell and its drafters said so. The question the Council of Europe’s lawyers put to themselves after February 1948 was how a democracy could be given warning that it was being taken over from inside by constitutional means, which is what had just happened in Czechoslovakia; the catalogue of rights is short, classical and political for that reason, and the collective enforcement machinery is the answer to a state that would not police itself. The claim is about the drafting purpose and the shape it produced. It is not a claim that the convention was made only for that, and the Convention was also the European answer to the Universal Declaration of the year before.
explanations.1948-czechoslovak-coup-d-etat--nato-foun: Prague in February 1948 is the event that turned a discussion into a treaty. A parliamentary state with a communist minority in coalition became a one-party state in a fortnight, and the governments of western Europe read it as a description of what could be done to them; the Brussels treaty was signed three weeks later, the Vandenberg resolution passed in June, and the negotiations that produced the North Atlantic treaty began in the same months. Portugal signed that treaty in April 1949, a dictatorship among democracies and admitted for the Azores. The claim is about the timing and the urgency, not about the American decision to commit, which Greece had already produced.
explanations.1949-portuguese-presidential-election--d: Norton de Matos’s campaign showed the opposition that a presidential election was the one moment at which the regime had to let it speak in public, and showed the regime that the moment could be closed by persecution stopping short of an outright ban. Delgado ran the same manoeuvre nine years later and pushed it past what the regime had allowed for — which is why it ended not in another withdrawal but in the abolition of the direct election itself.
explanations.1952-egyptian-revolution--2011-egyptian-: The English article on the revolution of 2011 traces the system it rose against to 1952: Mubarak became president after the assassination of Sadat in 1981 and inherited an authoritarian system imposed in 1952 following the coup against King Farouk, which abolished the monarchy and made Egypt a military-dominated one-party state; he was in the thirtieth year of his regime when the uprising began.
explanations.1952-egyptian-revolution--algerian-war--: Cairo after 1952 is where the Algerian revolution was prepared and from where it was supplied. The external delegation of the FLN sat there, the Voice of the Arabs broadcast to the Maghreb, and the first arms came through Egypt and Libya; Nasser’s Egypt was both the sponsor and the standing demonstration that an Arab army could remove a king and see off an Anglo-French expedition. The claim is about the base and the example. The war of 1954 had Algerian causes, in the settler regime and the failure of assimilation, and this edge does not touch them.
explanations.1957-guinean-territorial-assembly-electi: A territory could only vote No to the French community if somebody in it had the standing to ask for a No, and this election is what gave Sékou Touré that standing: fifty-six of sixty seats, a territorial government, a party organisation reaching into every canton, and eighteen months to use them. Every other French African territory voted Yes. The atlas keeps a French election because the answer of September 1958 put an independent state on the border of Portuguese Guinea, and the war of 1963 was launched from it.
explanations.1964-brazilian-coup-detat--1985-brazilia: The college that ended the dictatorship was the dictatorship’s own machine. It had been built under the constitution of 1967–69 so that the candidate chosen by the High Command of the Armed Forces would always be elected; in 1985, with the negotiated transition already running, its members were placed under no coercion and chose whom they liked. The last indirect election and the last under military rule are the same election.
explanations.1964-brazilian-coup-detat--brazilian-mil: The English article on the dictatorship dates it from the coup: it was established on 1 April 1964, after a coup d’état by the Brazilian Armed Forces with support from the United States government against President João Goulart, and lasted twenty-one years, until 15 March 1985.
explanations.1964-brazilian-coup-detat--operation-bro: The operation was activated when the coup broke out. The task force was ordered out on 31 March and the Forrestal left Norfolk on 1 April; when Castelo Branco told Lincoln Gordon that logistical support would not be needed the order to disband came, at 17:22 on the 2nd. Read in this direction the edge says only what the record supports — the American movement followed the Brazilian one and was called off by it. What the Americans were answering, and why, is the disputed link into this same event.
explanations.1964-brazilian-coup-detat--the-1988-braz: The text is an answer to the regime the coup began. It replaced the autocratic constitution of 1967 and capped twenty-one years of military dictatorship, and it resignified the role of the state in citizens’ lives with a vast apparatus of human and individual rights protection — a list that reads as an inventory of what the twenty-one years had done. Read in this direction the edge says the constitution reacted to the coup, which is what its own drafters said they were doing.
explanations.1964-brazilian-coup-detat--the-brazilian: The debt was contracted by the governments the coup installed, for the industrialisation and infrastructure they had chosen, and on terms they accepted: between 1975 and 1982 Latin American debt to commercial banks grew at a cumulative 20.4 per cent a year, much of it in short-term loans without safeguards. The crisis is the bill for a policy, and the policy had one author.

After the coup the military was more concerned with political control and left economic policy to a group of trusted technocrats under Delfim Netto, and the model that followed rested on low wages, rising exports and inflows of foreign capital — three things a government answerable to an electorate would have found harder to hold together. James Petras’s reading, which Wikipedia carries, makes the seizure of power and the system of military-police control part of what the growth was built on. `enabled`: the regime did not produce ten per cent a year by decree, but it is what made that particular model available.
explanations.1965-portuguese-presidential-election--c: Under the 1933 constitution the president appointed and dismissed the head of government, and that was very nearly the whole of what the office could do. When Salazar was disabled by a stroke in September 1968 the decision was Tomás’s alone, and he made it: Caetano, rather than a hardliner or a caretaker, and made without consulting the man being replaced. The 1965 election is what put him there with a term running to 1972 and no one able to remove him.
explanations.1969-portuguese-legislative-election--19: In 1969 the opposition took Caetano’s invitation, campaigned under a loosened censorship, and was given nothing at all: 133,000 votes against 980,000 and not one seat, in a system where a third of the vote in a city is worth no representation whatever. The withdrawal of 1973 is the conclusion drawn from that experiment. The CDEs did not stand aside on principle — they had spent 1969 not standing aside — but because they had tested the opening and knew what it was worth.
explanations.1969-portuguese-legislative-election--ca: The opening of 1969 was real enough to be tested and narrow enough to fail the test. The opposition was allowed to campaign and then beaten by a system that made its votes worthless; the censorship returned within months; the liberal deputies elected inside the National Union found they could not legislate and were gone by 1973. What that closed was the civilian road out of the regime. The officers who acted in April 1974 did not need a theory that the Estado Novo could not reform itself with voters in the room — they had watched it try and stop.
explanations.1972-portuguese-presidential-election--c: Caetano had come in with a reputation for reform and spent five years discovering what he could not do, and the president was a substantial part of what he could not do: Tomás held the power to dismiss him and was understood on all sides to be the guarantor of the war being fought to the end. The election of July 1972 removed the one date on which that could have changed by ordinary means, putting his term beyond the reach of the regime's own calendar until 1979. The edge argues a closed door rather than an open one — the captains' movement of 1973 and 1974 grew out of a war nobody in office could end — and that is why it is `precondition-of`.
explanations.1973-chilean-coup-d-etat--1976-argentine: The claim here is a shared doctrine and a demonstration, not a chain of command. The junta of March 1976 took power with the same doctrine of national security the Chilean and Brazilian officers worked from, it organised its repression on a scale Chile had shown was survivable internationally, and the two co-operated in the surveillance and transfer of exiles that came to be called Condor. The Argentine coup had Argentine causes, a government that had lost control of prices and of its own armed left, and this edge does not claim otherwise. Marked probable: the doctrine was continental and Chile was its most visible case, not its only source.
explanations.1973-chilean-coup-d-etat--25-november-19: Chile is the case every side in Portugal argued from in 1975, and that is what this edge claims. For the far left and for much of the fifth provisional government, Allende’s fall was the proof that a revolution which left the armed forces and the economy intact would be destroyed, and the argument for moving faster. For the Socialists, for the moderate officers of the Group of Nine and for the Americans, it was the outcome to be avoided at almost any cost, and Kissinger’s remark that Soares was a Kerensky is the same reading from the other end. The confrontation of 25 November was made in Portugal by Portuguese quarrels; what Chile supplied was the frame in which everybody understood what they were doing. Inspired is used here for an example that was read as a warning, and the edge claims nothing more than that.
explanations.1973-portuguese-legislative-election--ca: This is narrower than the edge the atlas now carries from 1969, which is about the civilian road closing. What October 1973 added was finality and timing. The last Assembly of the Estado Novo was seated in November; the captains had begun meeting that September over a decree on seniority, and through the winter their grievance acquired a political programme and then a plan. After that autumn nobody in uniform had to be persuaded that the Assembly was not where the war would be ended. The claim is about how tight the sequence is, not that the election produced the coup.
explanations.1976-argentine-coup-d-etat--falklands-wa: The English article puts the decision inside the regime the coup installed: Argentina had been governed since 1976 by the military junta of the National Reorganisation Process, and by opting for military action the Galtieri government "hoped to mobilise the long-standing patriotic feelings of Argentines towards the islands, diverting public attention from the chronic economic problems and the ongoing human rights violations of its Dirty War, bolstering the junta’s dwindling legitimacy". The claim is that the junta the coup created is what took the decision, and no more: the article gives Admiral Anaya as the architect of the military solution and the sovereignty claim as long-standing.
explanations.1979-portuguese-legislative-election--co: Abolishing the Council of the Revolution meant amending the constitution, and amending it meant two thirds of the deputies. The Democratic Alliance had wanted the Council gone since before it was an alliance, and the election of 2 December 1979 — confirmed at the fresh election of October 1980 — is what put it in charge of the Assembly with the standing to demand the revision. Two thirds it did not have on its own: the text of 1982 was a bargain with the Socialists, and what the 1979 result bought was not the votes but the position from which the bargain could be forced.
explanations.1980-portuguese-legislative-election--co: The revision of 1982 was voted by the Assembly this election returned, and it needed two thirds of it. The Democratic Alliance had made abolishing the Council of the Revolution its purpose before it had a majority; what the ballot of 5 October 1980 gave it was a full four-year legislature in which to negotiate the two thirds with the Socialists rather than a remnant term running out in weeks. The atlas keeps this edge and the one from the election of December 1979 apart because they argue different things: 1979 put the alliance in a position to demand the revision, 1980 gave it the time to get it.
explanations.1980-portuguese-presidential-election--c: The revision of 1982 did two things at once: it abolished the Council of the Revolution, which everyone civilian wanted gone, and it trimmed the powers of a president the Assembly's majority had just failed to unseat. Eanes had been the Armed Forces Movement's man and had been re-elected in December 1980 against the alliance's own candidate, with four more years to run and the power to dismiss governments. Reading the revision only as the end of military tutelage misses the second half of it; this edge is the second half, and it is `reacted-to` rather than `caused` because the constitutional programme predates the election it was sharpened by.
explanations.1982-lebanon-war--2006-lebanon-war--enab: The party on one side of the 2006 war did not exist before the invasion of 1982. The English article on the 1982 war says that the Israeli occupation that followed it "saw the emergence of Hezbollah, an Iranian-backed Shia Islamist group", which waged a guerrilla war against that occupation until the final Israeli withdrawal in 2000; the article on the civil war says the same, that a radical turnover followed the invasion with the establishment of Hezbollah, whose stated object was to end the occupation. The 2006 war was fought between Hezbollah and Israel, and the article calls it the third Israeli invasion of Lebanon since 1978.
explanations.1982-lebanon-war--twelve-day-war--precon: The same background section dates the proxy conflict the war grew out of from that war: Israel has fought wars with Iranian proxies including against Hezbollah since the 1982 Lebanon war.
explanations.1983-portuguese-legislative-election--im: A Fund programme is a political act before it is a technical one: it needs a government able to survive the devaluation and the restriction it commits to. The two years before this election had produced neither — the alliance was breaking up and the payments position was deteriorating through it. The Bloco Central took office in June 1983 with the two largest parties inside it and went to the Fund in the autumn, which is the arrangement that made the programme possible and also the arrangement that made it survivable. Whether the recession that followed was worth it is argued about; that this government is what allowed the agreement to be signed is not.
explanations.1983-portuguese-legislative-election--tr: Portugal had been negotiating with the Communities since 1977 and the negotiation had stalled repeatedly, on agriculture, on the Community's own budget quarrel and on the instability of the governments doing the negotiating. The Bloco Central this election produced held for two years with both large parties committed to accession, and it is the government that closed the chapters and signed on 12 June 1985. The atlas argues the political condition rather than the diplomacy: the terms were the Community's, the ability to accept them was this election's.
explanations.1985-brazilian-presidential-election--th: The constitution was made in the light of the transition to democracy, written from scratch over two years and promulgated on 5 October 1988 — which is to say by the congress and the presidency the election of January 1985 produced, after Neves died and Sarney took office. The New Republic the text founds is named after that handover.
explanations.1985-portuguese-legislative-election--ca: The absolute majority of 1987 was not won from opposition: it was won by a government already in office, twenty-one months old, brought down by a censure motion the voters were then asked to judge. This election is what put that government there and what made it a minority — four parties in the Assembly and a fifth, the PRD, holding enough seats to deny anyone a majority. The atlas argues the sequence rather than an inevitability: without a minority Cavaco government there is no censure motion, and without the censure motion there is no election in July 1987 for a majority to be won at.
explanations.1991-portuguese-legislative-election--ex: A world exposition is a decade-long commitment of public money made by whoever holds the government when the bid is decided. Lisbon's bid was won in June 1992, eight months into the majority this election returned, and the site, the bridge, the metro extension and the expropriations along the eastern riverfront were all committed by that government before it lost office in 1995. Expo 98 opened under a different party, and this edge argues the decision rather than the opening: what the election settled was that there would be a government able to sign for it.
explanations.1991-soviet-coup-d-etat-attempt--belovez: The English article quotes one of the three signatories, Stanislav Shushkevich, saying in 2006 that by December the union had already been broken up by the putschists who in August 1991 had tried to remove Gorbachev from power to prevent the transformation of the Soviet Union into what he described as a confederation. The article reports that as a participant's account of why the three met, not as a settled finding.
explanations.1991-soviet-coup-d-etat-attempt--dissolu: The English article on the dissolution says the Soviet Union was formally dissolved and ceased to exist as a sovereign state on 26 December 1991, and that this brought an end to Gorbachev’s efforts to reform the Soviet political and economic system. The coup of August 1991 is what the record’s own retraction named as the neighbour it argued to, and it is four months before the date the article gives.
explanations.1995-portuguese-legislative-election--19: The English article sets the contest against the legislative result of the year before: the Social Democrats "were coming from a clear defeat in the 1995 Portuguese legislative election", and their former leader Aníbal Cavaco Silva, ten years prime minister, ran against the mayor of Lisbon Jorge Sampaio — a rematch of the legislative election of 1991. Sampaio won with nearly 54 per cent. The article gives the defeat as the position the right went in from and does not make it the cause of the outcome.
explanations.1995-portuguese-legislative-election--eu: Joining the single currency in the first wave meant hitting the Maastricht numbers on deficit, debt, inflation and rates in the reference year 1997, and then defending the decision politically. The government this election produced made that its central commitment and was in office for exactly the years the test covered. The atlas argues the political condition and not the arithmetic: the convergence had been under way since 1992 under the previous majority, and what changed in 1995 was not the direction but that the party that had opposed the Maastricht ratification now owned the target.
explanations.1995-portuguese-legislative-election--po: Administrative regions have been in the constitution since 1976 and have never existed. Creating them was a Socialist commitment carried into the 1995 campaign, and the government this election produced is what turned the commitment into a law of regional delimitation and then into the referendum of 8 November 1998. Nobody else would have called it: the Social Democrats campaigned against, the referendum failed on both questions, and no government has proposed regionalisation since. This edge is `caused` rather than `enabled` because the ballot exists for no other reason than that this government decided to hold it.
explanations.1998-portuguese-abortion-referendum--200: The referendum of 2007 is the same question as that of 1998, put again because the first answer had settled nothing: a margin of two points, on a turnout of under a third, against a law the Assembly had already passed. Both sides read 1998 as unfinished — the yes because it had lost narrowly on an abstention it blamed on the date and the campaign, the no because it had won without the turnout that would have bound anyone. Nine years is a long reaction, and the edge is `reacted-to` rather than `caused` for that reason: what 1998 produced was not the second ballot but the certainty that there would have to be one.
explanations.1999-macanese-chief-executive-election--: The transfer of 20 December 1999 handed the territory to a government, not to a vacancy, and that government had to exist before midnight. The joint declaration of 1987 provided for a Chief Executive chosen locally by a committee, and the choice of 15 May is what filled the post: from that day the region had a designated head, an administration in formation and a legal continuity to hand over into. The edge is `precondition-of` rather than `caused` because the handover's date and terms were fixed twelve years earlier and nothing about this ballot could have changed either.
explanations.25-november-1975--constitution-1976--ena: The end of the revolutionary period allowed the Constituent Assembly to complete a text that combined a democratic order with the military's residual guardianship through the Council of the Revolution.
explanations.25-november-1975--eanes-elected-1976--ca: Eanes was the officer who commanded the operation of 25 November, and it is that command which made him the candidate the parties of the centre and right could agree on seven months later. He entered the election as the man who had ended the revolutionary period.
explanations.algerian-war--angola-war-begins-1961--pr: Algeria is present at both ends of what happened in Angola in 1961. The Portuguese officer corps had spent the late 1950s reading the French literature of guerre révolutionnaire out of Algeria and Indochina, and the doctrine of counter-subversion it applied in the north — resettlement into aldeamentos, psychological action, the primacy of the political over the military — is that literature; the war ministry had begun the courses before the risings. And for the movements, Algeria was the standing demonstration that a European power governing a settler territory as part of itself could be fought. The claim is about doctrine and example on both sides, not that Algeria caused the risings of February and March: those had causes in Angola, in the coffee districts and in the city.
explanations.alvor-agreement-1975--angola-independenc: The agreement fixed the date, 11 November, and the terms on which Portugal would leave. That the transitional government collapsed and the three movements fought does not undo what Alvor settled: the handover happened on the day Alvor named.
explanations.amsterdam-treaty--euro-adoption-1999--pr: The single currency Portugal joined on 1 January 1999 was governed by rules settled at Amsterdam in June 1997: the stability and growth pact, agreed at that European Council and given legal form alongside the treaty, is what turned the Maastricht deficit criterion from a condition of entry into a standing obligation of membership, and it is the instrument Portuguese budgets were made against for the next fifteen years. The claim is about the rules of the currency and not about the decision to adopt it, which was taken at Maastricht and confirmed in 1998.
explanations.amsterdam-treaty--treaty-of-nice--precon: Nice exists because Amsterdam failed. The institutional questions that enlargement to the east made unavoidable, the size of the Commission, the weighting of votes in the Council and the extent of qualified majority, were on the Amsterdam agenda and were left over, in a protocol that said they would have to be settled before enlargement. The conference of 2000 settled them badly enough that the next treaty was begun immediately. The claim is that Nice is the second attempt at Amsterdam’s unfinished business, which is what both texts say of themselves.
explanations.anglo-irish-treaty--irish-civil-war--cau: The English article on the civil war says it was waged between the Provisional Government of Ireland and the anti-Treaty IRA over the Anglo-Irish Treaty: the Provisional Government supported the terms of the treaty, the anti-Treaty opposition saw it as a betrayal of the Irish Republic proclaimed during the Easter Rising of 1916, and many of the combatants had fought together against the British and divided once the treaty negotiations began. The article on the treaty says it concluded the Irish War of Independence and provided for the establishment of the Irish Free State as a self-governing dominion.
explanations.anglo-irish-treaty--the-troubles--precon: The English article on the treaty says it gave Northern Ireland, which had been created by the Government of Ireland Act 1920, an option to opt out of the Irish Free State, and that the Parliament of Northern Ireland exercised it. The article on the Troubles says the conflict was a political and nationalistic struggle fought over the status of Northern Ireland, unionists and loyalists wanting it to remain within the United Kingdom and nationalists and republicans wanting it to leave. The status the later conflict was fought over is the one the treaty left open; neither article calls the treaty its cause.
explanations.angola-independence-1975--angolan-civil-: The English article on the civil war dates it from the independence: the war began immediately after Angola became independent from Portugal in November 1975, as a power struggle between two former anti-colonial guerrilla movements, the MPLA and UNITA, which had different roots in Angolan society and mutually incompatible leaderships despite their shared aim of ending colonial rule.
explanations.angola-independence-1975--cplp-founding-: A community of Portuguese-speaking states could not exist while five of its members were Portuguese territory. Angola stands here for the whole of 1974 and 1975: Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, Cape Verde and São Tomé and Príncipe became states within the same two years, and the community founded in 1996 is made of them together with Portugal and Brazil. It is marked probable rather than consensus for two reasons. The first is that decolonisation made the body possible without making it at all likely — twenty-one years passed, and several attempts failed, before anyone founded it. The second is editorial: choosing Angola's independence as the anchor for five independences is this record's simplification, not a claim that Angola mattered more than the others.
explanations.angola-war-begins-1961--botelho-moniz-co: The move was made about the war and only about the war: its authors wanted a change of policy in Africa and judged that it required a change of head of government. It came within weeks of the risings, and Salazar answered it by taking the defence ministry himself.
explanations.angola-war-begins-1961--carnation-revolu: Thirteen years of war on three fronts exhausted the army, the treasury and the regime's legitimacy; the officers who overthrew the Estado Novo did so to end a war they judged unwinnable.
explanations.angola-war-begins-1961--goa-annexed-1961: Portugal's isolation and military commitment in Angola from early 1961 is argued to have made the annexation of Goa in December a lower-risk decision for India than it had been in the preceding decade.
explanations.angola-war-begins-1961--guinea-war-begin: The PAIGC had prepared its armed struggle independently, but the Angolan uprising of 1961 and the international attention it drew shaped the timing and the expectations of the other movements in the Portuguese empire.
explanations.angola-war-begins-1961--mozambique-war-b: FRELIMO, founded in 1962, moved to armed struggle in 1964 in the context set by Angola and Guinea; the Angolan precedent showed that the Portuguese state would not negotiate and that armed struggle could draw international support.
explanations.anti-comintern-pact--tripartite-pact--pr: The English article on the pact of 1940 puts the two in one series: the Tripartite Pact was, "together with the Anti-Comintern Pact and the Pact of Steel, one of a number of agreements between Germany, Japan, Italy, and other countries of the Axis powers governing their relationship", and "Germany and Japan technically became allies with the signing of Anti-Comintern Pact of 1936". The claim is that the alliance of 1940 was built on the alignment of 1936, which is what the article says, and not that the earlier pact caused the later one.
explanations.arab-revolt--treaty-of-sevres--precondit: Sèvres is where the Ottoman defeat the revolt helped to bring about was written down, and where what had been promised during it was disposed of. The Arab provinces the revolt had fought across were separated from the Ottoman state and put under mandate rather than gathered into the kingdom the McMahon letters had been read as offering. The claim is deliberately narrow: the revolt is one of the things that put those provinces on the table at Sèvres and not the only one, and the Allied war aims for the Ottoman partition are older than the rising and were not made by it.
explanations.armistice-of-mudros--treaty-of-sevres--p: The English article's lead puts the two in that order and in that relation: the armistice was followed by the occupation of Istanbul and the subsequent partitioning of the Ottoman Empire, and the Treaty of Sèvres of 10 August 1920, signed in the aftermath of the First World War, imposed harsh terms on the Ottoman Empire. The armistice is what opened the Straits and the capital to the Allies; the terms came later and are the treaty's, not the armistice's.
explanations.assassination-of-archduke-franz-ferdinan: The claim is about the trigger and the five weeks after it, not about the origins of the war. Vienna decided on war with Serbia within a fortnight of the killing, obtained Berlin's guarantee, and sent an ultimatum drafted so that it would be rejected; the mobilisations of the last week of July followed from that, and the war was general by 4 August. Why the powers were in a position where a murder could do this — the alliance blocs, the naval and colonial rivalries, the timetables that made mobilisation hard to stop — is a separate argument this edge does not make.
explanations.azores-agreement-1943--nato-founding-194: The Azores agreement made Portugal a strategic partner of the Western allies before the war ended; the archipelago's value in Atlantic defence is the usual explanation for the invitation of an authoritarian regime into the alliance in 1949.
explanations.batepa-massacre--1975-sao-tomean-legisla: Twenty-two years is too long for causation and the edge does not claim it. What Batepá did was furnish São Toméan nationalism with the thing it had not had — a grievance against the colonial state that every forro family could name — and the movement that formed in exile in the following decade dated itself from it, as the independent state has done ever since with the day of the martyrs. The ballot of July 1975 is the moment that movement took the islands, and this edge says that the claim it took them with was made at Batepá. `inspired` is the type in this atlas for exactly that relation, and the reason the five types exist.
explanations.battle-of-the-lys-1918--coup-28-may-1926: The war, and the Lys as its emblem, is argued to have politicised the officer corps, discredited the parliamentary Republic among the military, and produced the veterans and grievances that made 1926 possible.
explanations.belovezh-accords--dissolution-of-the-sov: The English article's first sentence is that the agreement declared that the Soviet Union had effectively ceased to exist and established the Commonwealth of Independent States in its place, signed near Viskuli in Belovezhskaya Pushcha on 8 December 1991 by the leaders of three of the four republics that had signed the 1922 treaty creating the USSR. explanations.black-september--lebanese-civil-war--pre: The English article says that after the fighting "Jordan allowed the fedayeen to relocate to Lebanon via Syria, where they later became involved in the Lebanese Civil War". explanations.bretton-woods-system--imf-agreement-1978: The Fund Portugal went to in 1978 is the Bretton Woods institution, and the terms it went on are the Bretton Woods terms: a standby credit against a programme of demand restraint and exchange-rate correction, negotiated with a body created at a conference Portugal was not at in 1944. This is the edge by which the whole post-war monetary order reaches this atlas. It claims only that the institution and its instrument are the ones the conference made; the Portuguese crisis of 1977 and 1978 had Portuguese causes, which are in the records around it.
explanations.british-russian-convention--world-war-i-: The English article says the convention "would eventually form a component of the Triple Entente", that the treaty furthered the Anglo-Russian interest in outflanking the German Empire, and that "for Britain and Russia, the agreement was important in establishing a diplomatic alignment that endured until the First World War". explanations.budapest-memorandum--russo-ukrainian-war: The same section of the same article gives the memorandum as the assurance of Ukraine’s territorial integrity and independence that Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States made in 1994, in the background it writes for a war fought over that territory from 2014. explanations.cabral-assassinated-1973--guinea-bissau-: On one reading the unilateral declaration eight months later was the movement's answer to the killing: proof that the PAIGC had survived the loss of its founder, and a way of turning international sympathy into recognition while it was still fresh.
explanations.caetano-succeeds-salazar-1968--1969-port: Caetano came to the presidency of the council in September 1968 with no title of his own — appointed by a president chosen by an assembly, to replace a man who had never resigned — and an election was the obvious way to acquire one. explanations.caetano-succeeds-salazar-1968--carnation: Caetano's promise of liberalisation raised expectations that the regime then failed to meet, and his inability to change colonial policy left the army without a political solution; the disillusion of the "Primavera Marcelista" is part of why the coup found so little resistance.

explanations.carnation-revolution-1974--alvor-agreeme: Decolonisation by negotiation was the revolution's own programme, and the Portuguese side at Alvor was the government the revolution had produced. There is no version of the agreement without the change of regime in Lisbon nine months earlier.
explanations.carnation-revolution-1974--angola-indepe: Decolonisation was the revolution's first purpose; the Alvor agreement and the withdrawal of November 1975 followed from the decision, taken in Lisbon in 1974, to end the war by granting independence.
explanations.carnation-revolution-1974--constituent-a: Free elections to a Constituent Assembly within a year were a commitment of the Armed Forces Movement programme; the election of 25 April 1975 fulfilled it.
explanations.carnation-revolution-1974--east-timor-in: The Portuguese withdrawal from Timor during 1975, and the civil conflict that followed, created the vacuum that Indonesia filled; the invasion is generally read as a consequence of decolonisation conducted without the means to guarantee the outcome.
explanations.carnation-revolution-1974--fiftieth-anni: The commemoration exists because of the coup it commemorates, and the form it takes — a solemn session of parliament, a march down the Avenida da Liberdade, a public holiday — was settled in the years immediately after 1974 and has been argued over at every round number since. explanations.carnation-revolution-1974--macau-handove: Post-1974 Portugal defined Macau as Chinese territory under Portuguese administration and negotiated the Joint Declaration of 1987 on that basis; the handover is the last act of the decolonisation the revolution began.
explanations.carnation-revolution-1974--nationalisati: The revolution created the Council of the Revolution and the political conditions in which the failed coup of 11 March 1975 could be answered with the nationalisation of the financial system.
explanations.carnation-revolution-1974--spinola-resig: Spínola was president because the revolution made him one, on terms he did not control: a programme he had not written and a Council of State full of officers who had. explanations.charter-of-the-united-nations--genocide-: The Charter is the machinery the convention was made in and the authority it was made under: the General Assembly resolved in December 1946 that genocide was a crime under international law, the Economic and Social Council had the text drafted, and the Assembly adopted it two years later. The claim is narrow on purpose, because this atlas will hold a good many United Nations instruments and the fact that the United Nations convened the conference is not by itself an argument about any of them. What makes it one here is that the convention is the first treaty the Charter’s human-rights clauses were turned into, and the precedent for everything of the kind that followed.
explanations.charter-of-the-united-nations--internati: The Charter committed members to promote human rights and did not say what they were or what would happen if a state ignored them; the Universal Declaration of 1948 said what they were and bound nobody; the covenants of 1966 are the third step, in which the same organisation turned the list into treaty obligations with reporting machinery attached. Twenty years passed between the second step and the third because the two blocs disagreed about whether civil and economic rights belonged in one instrument, which is why there are two covenants and not one. The claim is about that sequence and the body that carried it, not that 1945 made 1966 certain.
explanations.charter-of-the-united-nations--un-admiss: Article 4 makes admission a decision of the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council, which means a permanent member can hold an applicant out indefinitely — and from 1946 both blocs did exactly that, so that membership became a currency rather than a status. Portugal, refused for nine years, entered in December 1955 in a package of sixteen states agreed between the blocs to clear the backlog. The design of the Charter is why the admission took the form of a bargain over a list rather than a judgement on Portugal, and it is also why what Portugal found inside was an Assembly majority it could not veto.
explanations.chinese-civil-war--korean-war--precondit: Two things about June 1950 follow from the Communist victory of 1949. Kim Il-sung got Stalin's consent for the attack only after the People's Republic existed and could be presented as a guarantor, and the Korean veterans of the Chinese armies were transferred back to build his divisions; and when the United Nations force reached the Yalu in October, it was a Chinese state four months short of its first anniversary that sent a million men across the river. Without the outcome of 1949 neither the decision to attack nor the intervention that saved the North has its condition.
explanations.companhia-siderurgica-nacional-1941--pet: The second state company follows the first, and the argument for it was the argument the first had won: a strategic industry Brazil could not finance privately should be held by the state. CSN was created by Vargas’s decree and owned by the state for fifty years; Petrobras was created by a law Vargas sanctioned, against a draft statute of 1948 that would have opened oil to private capital at a time when world production was dominated by the Seven Sisters. `inspired` and not `caused`: what carried Law 2,004 was the campaign in the streets, and the precedent is what it had to point at.
explanations.companhia-siderurgica-nacional-1941--the: Both sit inside the same agreement. The steelworks was created after the Washington Accords between the Brazilian and American governments, and it is under the Washington Accords that Brazil undertook to raise Amazon latex production from eighteen thousand to forty-five thousand tons a year. The accords are the instrument in which what Brazil supplied and what Brazil received were written on the same page, and the steel side of it came first.
explanations.companhia-siderurgica-nacional-1941--us-: The hinge of the whole narrative: strategic commodities and strategic ground exchanged for industrial capital. Wikipedia states the sequence — in 1942, following the American proposal to finance the CSN, United States forces established air bases along Brazil’s north-eastern coast — and states the bargain: in exchange for raw materials the United States provided equipment, technical assistance and financing for a Brazilian steel mill, settled in July 1940. Roosevelt’s Good Neighbor policy is where the financing sat, and reports at the time said the United States had a plan to invade the Northeast if Vargas insisted on neutrality. What Brazil bought with the Atlantic narrows was the plant at Volta Redonda.

explanations.constitution-1911--pimenta-de-castro-gov: The 1911 constitution gave the president the power to appoint a head of government without a parliamentary majority behind him, and it is that power the president used in January 1915. Without it the Democrats could not have been excluded from office while holding the chamber.
explanations.constitution-1911--sidonio-pais-coup-191: Sidónio Pais presented his presidentialist regime explicitly as a remedy for the parliamentary supremacy and party dominance built into the 1911 settlement; the coup was a reaction against that constitutional order as much as against the government of the day.
explanations.constitution-1933--estado-novo-1933-1974: The English article on the Ditadura Nacional says the dictatorship lasted until the adoption of a new constitution in 1933 that ushered in the so-called Estado Novo; the article on the Estado Novo dates the corporatist state it describes to its installation in 1933.
explanations.constitution-1933--exposicao-mundo-portu: The exhibition was the regime displaying the account of the nation written into the 1933 settlement — imperial, Catholic, corporatist — and it needed the state that settlement had built to be staged at all: the funds, the ministries and the monopoly on public celebration.
explanations.constitution-1933--national-syndicalists: Once the regime had its own constitution, its own single party and its own corporative machinery, a rival movement offering the same things in a more excited form was a competitor rather than an ally, and the blue shirts had spent 1933 saying so out loud. The claim is about what the constitution made the National Syndicalists into, not that the constitution required their suppression in that particular year: the immediate occasion was the movement’s own agitation, and the sequence of 1934 and the revolt of 1935 are not records here. Marked probable, and the argument to check is whether the ban is better read as an act of the corporative settlement of 1933 or as an ordinary act of a police state against a movement it could not control.
explanations.constitution-1933--portugal-backs-franco: By 1936 the regime had a constitution, a single party and a police, and Salazar held the government firmly enough to commit the country to one side of a war next door without needing to argue it through a parliament. The help given to the Nationalists presupposes that concentration of decision.
explanations.constitution-1976--1976-azorean-regional: Autonomy for the Atlantic archipelagos is written into the constitution of 2 April 1976: the Azores and Madeira are autonomous regions with statutes of their own, a legislative assembly elected by their voters and a regional government answering to it. Nothing of the kind had existed under the Estado Novo, which ran the islands as districts. The assembly elected on 27 June is that clause taking physical form eleven weeks after the constitution came into force, and the date of the ballot — the same day as the presidential election — is itself the state hurrying to fill the institutions it had just created.
explanations.constitution-1976--1976-madeira-regional: The same clause of the constitution of 2 April 1976 that made the Azores an autonomous region made Madeira one, and on the same terms: a statute, an assembly its own voters elect, a government answering to that assembly. The ballot of 27 June is the first exercise of it. The atlas keeps the two archipelagos as separate events rather than one because the politics that followed them diverged almost at once, and because a reader following the constitution forward should arrive at two regions and not at an abstraction called autonomy.
explanations.constitution-1976--1976-portuguese-local: The constitution of 1976 makes local government an elected power of the state rather than an arm of the administration: freguesia, município and region are autarquias locais with their own organs, chosen by their own voters. The Estado Novo had appointed presidents of chambers, and the revolutionary period had run municipalities through administrative commissions named from the centre. The ballot of 12 December 1976 is the first time the constitutional clause was exercised, and everything the atlas holds under local elections after it descends from that clause and not from any of them.
explanations.constitution-1976--1979-portuguese-local: The clause that created elected local government in 1976 is what this ballot exercises, and the atlas wires it separately from the first exercise of that clause because the second time is when the thing became an institution rather than an act of foundation. The mandates run four years and the calendar is the constitution's, not the government's: 1979 falls a fortnight after a legislative election it had nothing to do with, and no local election since has been called by anybody.
explanations.constitution-1976--2006-portuguese-presi: The English article says the election was held to elect a successor to the incumbent President Jorge Sampaio, "who was barred from running for a third consecutive term by the Constitution of Portugal", and its background repeats it: re-elected in the first round in 2001, "because he was term-limited, he was forbidden by the Constitution to run for a third consecutive term". The two-term limit is why the sitting president was not a candidate; who replaced him is the record's own.
explanations.constitution-1976--constitutional-revisi: The Council of the Revolution abolished in 1982 was written into the 1976 text, as were the socialist commitments the revision softened. The revision is an argument with the constitution's own compromises, and it needed the amendment procedure the constitution itself provided.
explanations.constitution-1976--eanes-elected-1976--e: The directly elected presidency with its own powers is a creation of the 1976 text, and the June election is the first held under it. The office Eanes won did not exist in that form before April.
explanations.constitution-1976--eec-application-1977-: A democratic constitution was a precondition of membership under the Community's practice at the time; the application followed within a year of its entry into force.
explanations.constitution-1976--legislative-election-: The Assembly of the Republic elected on 25 April 1976 is the body the constitution created three weeks earlier, elected under the rules it laid down. The constituent assembly's work is the reason there was an ordinary parliament to elect at all.
explanations.constitutional-revision-1959--1965-portu: The revision of 1959 abolished the direct election of the president and gave the choice to an electoral college the regime controlled. The election of July 1965 is the first one held that way, and it is the revision working exactly as intended: no campaign, no crowds, no count to dispute, and the same admiral returned for another seven years.
explanations.constitutional-revision-1982--eec-access: Removing military tutelage from the constitution mattered to the negotiation: what Portugal offered the Community was a democracy of the ordinary kind, and a council of officers with power over legislation sat badly with that claim.
explanations.constitutional-revision-1982--soares-ele: The revision reduced the presidency to an office a civilian could hold without the armed forces behind him, and dissolved the body that had made the presidency a military post in practice. explanations.constitutionalization-attempts-in-iran--: This edge states its own gap and should be read carefully. What the constitutional revolution left behind, and what 1979 used, are two things: the fundamental law of 1906 and its supplement, which the opposition of the 1970s kept demanding the shah obey rather than demanding a new constitution, and the precedent of a clergy in politics on the side of the constitutionalists. The claim is about that inheritance and not about a continuous movement, which there was not. Marked probable, and the missing record that would carry most of the weight is 1953.
explanations.continuation-war--lapland-war--caused: The Lapland War is what the terms of leaving the Continuation War required. The Finns fought their former co-belligerent because the peace they had just made said they must.
explanations.coup-28-may-1926--1928-portuguese-presid: The Military Dictatorship had governed for close to two years with no title but the one it took in May 1926, and its search for a form ran through the presidency. explanations.coup-28-may-1926--constitution-1933--pre: The Estado Novo was built inside the Military Dictatorship that 28 May created; the 1933 constitution formalised a state of exception that had lasted seven years.
explanations.coup-28-may-1926--ditadura-nacional-1926: The English article on the Ditadura Nacional defines it by the coup: it was the regime that governed Portugal from the end of the First Portuguese Republic with the 28 May 1926 coup d’état until the adoption of a new constitution in 1933.
explanations.coup-28-may-1926--salazar-finance-minist: The Military Dictatorship's failure to balance the budget or obtain a foreign loan on acceptable terms led it to call Salazar in 1928 and accept his conditions; without the dictatorship there was no such vacancy and no such power.
explanations.coup-attempt-11-march-1975--nationalisat: The banks and insurance companies were taken over three days later, and the reason given was the failed coup: the groups that owned them were named as its financiers. explanations.croatian-war-of-independence--croat-bosn: The English article's background says that from July 1991 to January 1992, during the Croatian War of Independence, the JNA and Serb paramilitaries used Bosnian territory to wage attacks on Croatia, and that the Croatian government began arming Croats in the Herzegovina region as early as October or November 1991, expecting that the Serbs would spread the war into Bosnia and Herzegovina; the article hangs that expectation on Goldstein 1999, page 243, which is the second author here. By late 1991 about 20,000 Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina had enlisted in the Croatian National Guard.
explanations.cuban-revolution--angola-independence-19: Which of the three movements held Luanda at midnight on 11 November 1975 was settled in the field in the six weeks before it, and what settled it was the arrival of Cuban regular troops and artillery against the FNLA column from the north and the South African one from the south. explanations.cultural-revolution--sino-soviet-border-: The English article says of the March 1969 attack on Zhenbao Island that "historians have suggested Mao provoked the clash to further the radical sentiments of the Cultural Revolution or to elevate China's international standing towards the Cold War's two superpowers". explanations.delgado-candidacy-1958--constitutional-r: The revision removed the very mechanism that had produced the shock: direct election of the president. explanations.delgado-candidacy-1958--delgado-assassin: The candidacy is what made Delgado the regime's principal enemy and kept him one in exile; the PIDE operation of 1965 was aimed at the man the 1958 campaign had created. Without it he would have been one more exiled officer.
explanations.delgado-candidacy-1958--santa-maria-hija: The 1958 campaign showed the opposition how much attention a single public confrontation could draw and then, in its defeat, that the legal road was closed. explanations.dissolution-of-the-soviet-union--1993-ru: The article on the dissolution says it ended the Soviet Union’s federal government as well as the state. explanations.dissolution-of-the-soviet-union--budapes: The English article on the Russo-Ukrainian war says that after the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991 Ukraine signed the Non-Proliferation Treaty in 1994 and agreed to give up the former Soviet nuclear weapons on its territory, and that in return Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States agreed to uphold Ukraine’s territorial integrity and independence through the Budapest Memorandum on Security Assurances. explanations.dissolution-of-the-soviet-union--russo-u: The English article on the war begins its background with the dissolution: after the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, Ukraine and Russia maintained ties, and in 1994 Ukraine signed the Non-Proliferation Treaty and agreed to give up the former Soviet nuclear weapons on its territory, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States agreeing in return to uphold Ukraine’s territorial integrity and independence through the Budapest Memorandum. explanations.ditadura-nacional-1926-1933--estado-novo: The English article on the Estado Novo says it evolved from the Ditadura Nacional formed after the coup of 28 May 1926 against the unstable First Republic, and that historians recognise the two together as the Second Portuguese Republic. explanations.east-timor-invasion-1975--east-timor-ind: The independence of 2002 resolved the occupation that began in 1975; the referendum of 1999 and the United Nations administration were responses to that occupation and its resistance.
explanations.east-timor-invasion-1975--hat-nipah-and-: The landing at Dili on 7 December 1975 opened a war in the interior that lasted a quarter of a century, and these killings are dated to its fifth and sixth weeks, in towns south of the capital along the line the occupation was pushing inland. explanations.easter-rising--irish-civil-war--precondi: This edge states its own gap. What survives the gap is real. The Rising made the republic that was declared in 1916 the thing republicans were bound to, and the civil war of 1922 was fought over whether the Free State the Treaty offered was that republic or a betrayal of it, by men who had been on the same side in 1916. Until the Treaty is a record here, this edge is the only route between the two and it should be read as a placeholder for three.
explanations.eastern-front--potsdam-conference--preco: What the three governments could settle at Potsdam in July 1945 was bounded by where their armies already were, and in the east that was the Red Army's doing: Poland's frontiers were moved west onto ground the Soviet Union held, the German population east of the Oder-Neisse was expelled with Allied consent, and the occupation zones were drawn around lines the fighting had fixed. The conference ratified a distribution of force rather than creating one. That is a claim about the limits of the negotiation, not about the intentions of the negotiators.
explanations.eec-accession-1986--1987-european-parlia: There is no Portuguese seat in the European Parliament before 1 January 1986, and for the first eighteen months the twenty-four seats accession created were filled by delegates the Assembly of the Republic appointed from among its own members. The ballot of 19 July 1987 is the first time those seats were elected, and it exists because of the accession and for no other reason. What the atlas gets from the edge is the interval: a year and a half in which the country was represented in a parliament its voters had not chosen.
explanations.eec-accession-1986--cavaco-absolute-majo: One reading credits accession: the funds, the growth and the sense that the country had arrived somewhere gave the government of 1985 a record to run on, and the majority of 1987 rewarded it.
explanations.eec-accession-1986--euro-adoption-1999--: Membership of the Community was the condition of membership of its monetary union, and the convergence Portugal ran through in the 1990s was set by treaties it had signed as a member. There is no route to the euro that does not pass through 1986.
explanations.eec-accession-1986--expo-98--enabled: The exhibition was built with Community structural funds and by the administrative machinery that a decade of them had produced, on the model of public works Portugal had been running since accession. It is hard to imagine the scale of it in the economy of 1985.
explanations.eec-accession-1986--schengen-in-force-19: Schengen was an agreement among member states of the European Communities, made outside the Community treaties but not outside the Community: only members were party to it, and Portugal had been one for five years when it signed in 1991. The precondition is institutional rather than causal — accession did not make Portugal want an open border with Spain, and Lisbon and Madrid had their own reasons for wanting one — but without accession there would have been nothing for Portugal to sign. That much is not in dispute, which is why it is marked consensus. The question this link does not answer is why the two Iberian states joined the first wave instead of waiting to see how it worked.
explanations.eec-accession-1986--troika-bailout-2011-: One line of argument holds that integration and later the euro removed the exchange-rate adjustment and cheapened credit, producing the debt accumulation and loss of competitiveness that ended in the 2011 request for assistance.
explanations.eec-application-1977--eec-accession-1986: Accession in 1986 was the outcome of the negotiation opened by the 1977 application, prolonged by the Community's own difficulties and by the parallel Spanish application.
explanations.efta-accession-1960--eec-application-197: The application of 1977 was a political act of the new democracy, but the economic ground it stood on had been laid seventeen years earlier. By then the Community was already Portugal's largest market, Portuguese industry had lived with scheduled tariff reduction for a generation, and the apparatus for negotiating access existed because the association had required one — as had the free trade agreement with the Community that followed in 1972. The link is a precondition and emphatically not a cause: the Estado Novo chose the association precisely so as not to have to join the Community, and would not have made the 1977 application. What is argued about is the weight — whether the association prepared Portugal for Europe or merely postponed the choice by seventeen years — which is why this is probable and not consensus.
explanations.estado-novo-1933-1974--portuguese-coloni: The English article on the colonial war puts the regime at the centre of why it happened at all: unlike other European nations during the 1950s and 1960s, the Portuguese Estado Novo regime did not withdraw from its African territories, and the thirteen-year conflict from 1961 was fought between Portugal’s military and the nationalist movements that became active there during the 1960s.
explanations.euro-adoption-1999--crisis-portugal--pre: This is the argument Ricardo Reis makes about the Portuguese slump: that the capital which flowed in after the escudo was fixed and the euro adopted went disproportionately into non-tradable sectors, that productivity did not follow it, and that the debt built in those years is what made the country unable to refinance itself when lending stopped in 2010. The atlas already draws the same line from the euro to the bailout of 2011; drawn here it says the same thing one step earlier, at the crisis rather than at the rescue. Probable, not consensus: the weight the euro decade carries against the recession of 2008 is a live argument among economists, and this record was drafted without reading either side at length.
explanations.euro-adoption-1999--troika-bailout-2011-: On one account the euro is the mechanism of the crisis: interest rates far below what Portugal had known drew in a decade of capital that went into non-tradable sectors, productivity stalled, and when the flow stopped the country had neither the growth to service the debt nor a currency to devalue.
explanations.february-revolution--october-revolution-: February did not make October, but it made the two things October used. It created the soviet, an assembly with real authority over the garrison and the railways and no responsibility for governing, which is the instrument the Bolsheviks took Petrograd with in October; and it left the Provisional Government committed to continuing the war, which is the commitment that emptied it of support through the summer. The Kornilov affair in August then armed the Bolsheviks and discredited the government at once. Whether October was a revolution or a coup is argued elsewhere; this edge only says that February set the field it was played on.
explanations.first-balkan-war--assassination-of-archd: Between October 1912 and May 1913 the Ottoman Empire lost nearly everything it still held in Europe, and the South Slav question took the shape it had in 1914: not a question of Ottoman misgovernment but of who would inherit, with Serbia doubled and Austria-Hungary facing a neighbour that spoke for the Slavs inside its own borders. Sarajevo happened inside that question. The claim is about the ground the assassination stood on, not about the plot, which was Bosnian and had its own history.
explanations.first-balkan-war--second-balkan-war--cau: The second war was fought over the spoils of the first. The Balkan League had agreed how to divide Ottoman Europe before it went to war and could not hold to it once it had won: Serbia, denied the Adriatic coast by the powers, wanted compensation in the Macedonian districts promised to Bulgaria, Greece had taken Salonika, and Bulgaria attacked its allies on 29 June 1913 rather than accept arbitration. The claim is the ordinary one and it is narrow: the first war did not make the second inevitable, it made the quarrel that the second was about.
explanations.first-indochina-war--algerian-war--preco: The Algerian insurrection opened on 1 November 1954, three months after the Geneva agreements and six after Dien Bien Phu, and the men who opened it said what the timing meant: a European army had been beaten in the field by a colonial one, and the French Republic had accepted the result. The claim is about the demonstration and the moment, not that Indochina produced the Algerian nationalist movement, which had its own history running back to the 1930s and to the massacres at Sétif in 1945. What Indochina supplied was the evidence that the thing could be done.
explanations.first-indochina-war--geneva-conference--: The Indochinese half of the conference is the half that produced agreements, and it produced them because Dien Bien Phu fell on 7 May 1954, the day after the Indochina session opened. Eight years of war had exhausted a French government that changed while the conference sat; the accords of 20 July partitioned Vietnam at the seventeenth parallel, provided for elections in two years, and took France out. The claim is that the war brought the conference to that point and set what it had to decide.
explanations.first-indochina-war--vietnam-war--precon: Geneva ended the French war by dividing Vietnam at the seventeenth parallel as a temporary military line, with national elections promised for 1956 that the southern government and the United States then refused to hold. Everything the second war was fought over is in that arrangement: a partition treated as a frontier, a northern state that regarded the country as unfinished, and a southern one whose legitimacy rested on an election that never took place. The American commitment that followed is a further step this edge does not make.
explanations.first-sudanese-civil-war--second-sudanes: The English article says the Addis Ababa Agreement ended the war in 1972 but "failed to completely dispel the tensions and addressed only some of the issues stated by southern Sudan", and that "the breakdown of the initial appeasement later led to a reigniting of the north–south conflict during the Second Sudanese Civil War". Its account of the aftermath repeats it: infringements by the north increased social unrest in the south in the mid-1970s, leading to the 1983 army mutiny that sparked the second war.
explanations.geneva-conference--algerian-war--precond: Three months separate the accords of 20 July 1954 from the risings of 1 November, and the connection between them is not a coincidence but it is not a simple cause either. Two things carried over. The first is the army: the officers who had lost Indochina went to Algeria with a doctrine of revolutionary war worked out against the Viet Minh and a determination that this would not be lost as well, which is the doctrine Portuguese officers later studied for Angola. The second is the demonstration, for the Algerians, that a colonial power could be beaten in the field. The claim is about the transfer of the doctrine and the example, and it is marked probable because the rising had been planned before Geneva.
explanations.geneva-conference--vietnam-war--precondi: The line at the seventeenth parallel that the accords drew as a military demarcation became a border because the elections they provided for in 1956 were never held, and the war of the following twenty years was fought across it. The United States did not sign the final declaration and undertook only not to disturb it by force. The claim is that Geneva made the partition the later war was about; it is not a claim that Geneva caused the war, which needed the refusal of the elections and an American commitment neither of which the conference decided.
explanations.genocide-convention--rome-statute-of-the: The English article on the statute begins its history with the convention: General Assembly resolution 260 of 9 December 1948, the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, "was the first step toward the establishment of an international permanent criminal tribunal with jurisdiction on crimes yet to be defined in international treaties", and the resolution expressed the hope that the UN legal commission would work in that direction. The article on the convention says from the other side that its definition of genocide has been adopted by international and hybrid tribunals, the International Criminal Court among them.
explanations.german-revolution-of-1918-1919--treaty-o: The Allies would not sign with the Empire, and the revolution is what put something else in its place. The republic proclaimed on 9 November 1918 provided the government that asked for the armistice two days later, the delegation that went to Versailles, and the National Assembly that voted to accept the treaty in June 1919. The claim is about who could be treated with, not about the terms: those were settled in Paris among the victors, and the German republic was not at the table where they were made.
explanations.germany-declares-war-1916--battle-of-the: Belligerency led directly to the dispatch of the Portuguese Expeditionary Corps to Flanders in 1917; the corps was on the Lys because Portugal was at war.
explanations.germany-declares-war-1916--sidonio-pais-: Entry into the war was the policy of the Democratic party and was unpopular with much of the army and the public; the December 1917 coup drew its support from opposition to the war and to the government that had chosen it.
explanations.great-depression--bretton-woods-system--: Bretton Woods was designed against the 1930s and against nothing else. The fixed but adjustable parities, the fund that would lend a country in deficit rather than leave it to devalue, and the prohibition on the competitive devaluation and the bilateral clearing that had broken world trade after 1931 are all answers to what the delegates had lived through. The claim is that the depression set the problem the conference was convened to solve; it is not a claim about which of the two plans on the table, the American or the British, the answer was taken from.
explanations.great-depression--salazar-president-of-c: Salazar came to the presidency of the Council on a reputation made entirely of public accounts: he had balanced the budget from 1928 and he kept it balanced through the slump, while the currencies and the governments of the parliamentary states failed one after another. The argument here is about the political value of that record, not about the economy — Portugal's slump was comparatively shallow because the economy was poor, agricultural and barely exposed to short-term foreign lending, and the credit for that belongs less to the minister than the regime claimed. What the Depression supplied was the contrast that made the claim credible, at home and abroad, at the moment the military dictatorship had to choose a civilian form.
explanations.greek-civil-war--nato-founding-1949--pre: Greece is where the American commitment to defend Europe west of the Soviet line was first made and first paid for. Britain told Washington in February 1947 that it could no longer carry Greece and Turkey; the Truman doctrine of 12 March is the answer, and the Atlantic treaty of April 1949 is that answer turned into an alliance with a European membership. Portugal was a founder of it, which is why this edge reaches this atlas at all. The claim is about the commitment and not about the drafting: the treaty was negotiated over Berlin and Prague as much as over Greece, and those belong to the other edges around this one.
explanations.guinea-bissau-declares-independence-1973: Spínola had governed and commanded in Guinea from 1968 to 1973 and had concluded that the war could not be won; the PAIGC declaration and its international recognition confirmed the argument his book made public five months later.
explanations.guinea-war-begins-1963--cabral-assassina: Ten years of war made Cabral the most exposed figure of the Portuguese-African movements and made the PAIGC an organisation with its own internal quarrels over command and over the place of Cape Verdeans in it. Both the motive alleged of the killers and the motive alleged of Lisbon come out of that decade.
explanations.guinea-war-begins-1963--carnation-revolu: The Armed Forces Movement originated among the officers who had served in Guinea, the front where defeat seemed nearest; the specific grievances of that war shaped the conspiracy.
