explanations.guinea-war-begins-1963--guinea-bissau-de: Ten years of war left the PAIGC in control of much of the territory and able to proclaim a state that other governments recognised; the declaration was the political outcome of the military situation.
explanations.guinean-constitutional-referendum-1958--: This is narrower than the edge the atlas already carries into Cabral’s death from the war, and it is about exile rather than about geography. Cabral was shot in Conakry in January 1973 by men of his own movement, in a plot the Portuguese political police had worked at from outside. Those are the conditions of a liberation leadership that had spent a decade quartered in somebody else’s capital, with its ranks, its rivalries and its own security all maintained abroad and none of them answerable to a population it governed. The sanctuary that made the war possible is the same arrangement that left the movement open at its head.

A guerrilla war against a colonial power needs ground the power cannot enter. Guinea’s No in 1958 produced, along Portuguese Guinea’s southern border, an independent state whose government was willing to house the PAIGC: Conakry became its headquarters, its training camp, its arms route and the address from which it argued its case abroad. The party had existed since 1956 and had already tried the towns — the dockers’ strike at Pidjiguiti was shot down in 1959 — and what it did not have until Conakry was a rear it could not be driven out of. The war that opened in 1963 was fought from there.
explanations.gulf-war--iraq-war--precondition-of: The 1991 war ended without ending: a regime left standing, a ceasefire whose disarmament conditions were the legal ground everything afterwards was argued on, twelve years of sanctions and inspections, and no-fly zones patrolled by the same two air forces that opened the war of 2003. That is why the case made in 2002 could be put as enforcement of an old resolution rather than as a new war, and why the American and British governments had the standing deployments to act quickly. The claim is about the unfinished settlement, not that 2003 followed from 1991: the decision of 2003 had its own causes and September 2001 is among them.
explanations.iberian-pact--azores-agreement-1943--pre: Leasing bases in the Azores to Britain in August 1943 was the largest risk Salazar took in the war: it broke the appearance of neutrality in front of a Germany that had been standing on the Pyrenees since the previous November. He could take it because the peninsula behind him was closed. The pact of 1939, its protocol of 1940 and the Iberian bloc of 1942 had made Spain a neutral that would neither march nor be marched through, and without that the islands would have been a hostage rather than a card. The claim is about what made the concession survivable, not about what made Britain ask for it.
explanations.iberian-pact--treaty-of-friendship-and-c: The treaty of 1977 was drawn up to replace the Iberian Pact of 1939 and names the instrument it supersedes. What it answers is the pact’s content as much as its existence — an agreement between two dictators to leave each other alone, made when neither state had a foreign policy its people had any part in. Two democratic prime ministers signing a treaty of friendship and cooperation in November 1977, in the same year both governments applied to the European Communities, is a deliberate answer to that: the same neighbourly non-interference, resting on something else.
explanations.ilinden-preobrazhenie-uprising--young-tu: The English article on the revolution draws the line the atlas could not read before: "In response to the Ilinden Uprising of 1903, the Ottoman Empire capitulated to international pressure to implement reforms in Macedonia, known as the Mürzsteg program, under Great Power supervision, offending Muslims living in Macedonia and especially army officers." Those officers are the ones the article then describes making the revolution out of the Salonica-based Third Army. The claim is the article’s and it is narrow: the rising produced the foreign supervision the officers resented, not the revolution itself.
explanations.imf-agreement-1978--imf-agreement-1983--: The 1978 programme stabilised the external accounts without changing what produced them, and the same imbalance reappeared once restraint was relaxed. The second programme was, in its own terms, a second attempt at the first one's problem.
explanations.imf-agreement-1983--eec-accession-1986--: Accession required an economy the Community could admit, and the adjustment of 1983 to 1985 — devaluation, restriction, a current account brought back to balance — is what produced one. The negotiation closed as the programme ended.
explanations.indo-pakistani-war-of-1965--bangladesh-l: The war was fought in the west, over Kashmir, and left the eastern province defended by a single division and a promise. Mujibur Rahman put the Six Points to the Awami League in February 1966, four months after Tashkent, and the first of the arguments for them was that East Pakistan had been shown to be indefensible under a government that spent its army and its budget on the other frontier. From that programme come the election of 1970, the refusal to seat its winners, Operation Searchlight and the war. The claim is about where the autonomy movement got its decisive argument, not that 1965 made 1971 inevitable.
explanations.iran-iraq-war--gulf-war--precondition-of: The English article on the Gulf war traces the invasion of Kuwait to what the earlier war left behind: by the time the ceasefire with Iran was signed in August 1988, Iraq was heavily debt-ridden, most of that debt owed to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, with the debts to Kuwait alone amounting to fourteen billion dollars, and Iraq pressed both to forgive them and was refused. The article adds that Kuwait was overproducing oil at least in part to repair losses caused by Iranian attacks during the war, and that the resulting slump in the price cost Iraq seven billion dollars a year — the grievance the Iraqi government described as economic warfare.
explanations.iranian-revolution--2025-2026-iranian-pr: What is being protested against is the constitutional order the revolution built. The rial's collapse, the inflation and the shortages are the occasion, but the demands reported are not about a minister or a budget: they are about the system in which an unelected jurist stands above the elected government, and the crackdown the lead describes was ordered from that office. The lead itself measures the rising against 1979, which is the comparison the participants make. The claim is that the revolution created the state and the office now in question, not that it made these protests inevitable.
explanations.iranian-revolution--imf-agreement-1983--: The second oil shock is the revolution's: Iranian production collapsed through 1979 and the price of crude roughly doubled again, and the industrial world answered with the interest rates that produced the recession of 1980–82. Portugal met that with an economy that had not recovered from the first shock and a currency it was devaluing on a crawling peg, and the payments crisis of 1982–83 followed. As with 1978, the claim is that the external shock is one cause among several — the spending of the 1980 and 1981 governments is the other, and that argument belongs on the Portuguese records — and that this one came from Tehran.
explanations.iranian-revolution--iran-iraq-war--cause: The English article on the war gives the revolution as the first of Iraq’s reasons for starting it: in starting the war the Iraqi government, led by Saddam Hussein, primarily wanted to prevent Ruhollah Khomeini, Iran’s leader following the 1979 Iranian Revolution, from exporting Iran’s new state ideology to Iraq, and feared that Iran, a theocratic state mostly composed of Shia Muslims, would rally Iraq’s Shia majority against the Sunni-controlled Baʻathist government. The article names older border disputes beside it, which is why the link is probable.
explanations.iranian-revolution--mahsa-amini-protests: The protests of September 2022 were against the republic the revolution founded and against one of its founding acts in particular. Compulsory hijab was imposed in the first years after 1979 and the morality patrol that enforced it is an organ of that state; a woman died in its custody and the slogan that followed named the system, not the patrol. The claim is that the object of the protest is the order of 1979. It is not a claim that the revolution caused the protest, which needed forty years of its own.
explanations.iranian-revolution--twelve-day-war--prec: The English article on the war of June 2025 begins its background with the revolution: Israel maintained a close relationship with the Pahlavi monarchy until the Iranian Revolution, when the monarchy was ousted and replaced by an anti-Western theocratic Islamic republic led by Ruhollah Khomeini, and ever since, Iran’s government has repeatedly pledged to destroy Israel.
explanations.kashmir-conflict--indo-pakistani-war-of-: The English article on the conflict says that in 1965 Pakistan attempted to infiltrate Indian-administered Kashmir to precipitate an insurgency there, and that this resulted in another war fought by the two countries over the region. The article on the war says the same from the other end: although other border disputes existed, the Kashmir conflict was the predominant issue dividing the two states, and Pakistan believed the population of Kashmir was discontented with Indian rule and that a resistance movement could be ignited by a few infiltrating saboteurs.
explanations.kashmir-conflict--kargil-war--caused: The English article on the conflict lists Kargil among its wars: in 1999 armed conflict between the two countries broke out again in Kargil, with no effect on the status quo. The article on the war says it was triggered by the infiltration of Pakistani troops, disguised as Kashmiri militants, into positions on the Indian side of the Line of Control, which is the de facto border in the disputed region of Kashmir. The war is the conflict continued by other means and the article treats it as such.
explanations.katyn-massacre--warsaw-uprising--precond: The Home Army rose in August 1944 to take Warsaw before the Red Army reached it, so that Poland would be liberated by its own government rather than handed a new one — and the reason that had become the object was Katyn. The discovery of the graves in April 1943 and the Polish request for a Red Cross investigation gave Moscow the pretext to break with the London government, after which a rival Polish administration was assembled under Soviet auspices. The rising was an answer to that position. Whether the Red Army halted at the Vistula for military or political reasons is disputed and is not decided here.
explanations.kellogg-briand-pact--charter-of-the-unit: The pact of 1928 is where the renunciation of war as an instrument of policy was first written into a general treaty, and it is the text the Charter of 1945 rewrote with an enforcement machinery behind it. Between the two stands the use the pact was put to at Nuremberg, where the charge of crimes against peace rested on the argument that aggressive war had already been unlawful since 1928. The claim is about the lineage of the prohibition and is narrow: the pact had no sanction, failed at every test between 1931 and 1939, and is a precondition of the Charter rather than a cause of it.
explanations.korean-war--geneva-conference--caused: The conference of April to July 1954 was convened to settle what the armistice of Panmunjom had left open: the armistice had stopped the fighting and settled nothing about Korea’s future, and the Berlin conference of February 1954 agreed to take the Korean question to Geneva. That half of the conference ended without adopting anything, which is a result and belongs in the record. The claim is about why the conference met, not about what it achieved in Korea, which was nothing.
explanations.korean-war--korean-armistice-agreement--: The English article opens by saying the armistice "brought about a cessation of hostilities of the Korean War", signed on 27 July 1953 by the United Nations Command, the Korean People's Army and the Chinese People's Volunteer Army, and designed to ensure a complete cessation of hostilities "until a final peaceful settlement is achieved". This is the atlas's existing shape for a war and the instrument that ends it, as `spanish-american-war-1898 --caused--> treaty-of-paris-1898` already is.
explanations.korean-war--treaty-of-san-francisco--pre: Korea is why the peace with Japan was made in 1951 rather than later, and why it was made on those terms. The war turned the occupied country into the base the war was fought from and the workshop that supplied it, and an ally worth having was worth more to Washington than reparations or restrictions; Dulles negotiated the treaty and the security treaty together while the fighting went on. The claim is about the timing and the generosity, not about the fact of a peace, which had to come sooner or later.
explanations.kosovo-war--2008-kosovo-declaration-of-i: The English article says that after the end of the Kosovo War in 1999 the Security Council adopted Resolution 1244, which placed Kosovo under transitional United Nations administration, demanded the withdrawal of Serbian security forces and "envisioned an eventual UN-facilitated political process to resolve the status of Kosovo"; and that international negotiations on the final status began in 2006 "as envisaged under UN Security Council Resolution 1244 which ended the Kosovo conflict of 1999". The declaration of 17 February 2008 is the end of that process.
explanations.law-of-separation-1911--coup-28-may-1926: The religious question gave the Republic a permanent rural and Catholic opposition and fed the conservative currents that welcomed military intervention in 1926. It is one of several long-run conditions, not a trigger.
explanations.lebanese-civil-war--1982-lebanon-war--en: The English article on the 1982 war puts the invasion inside the civil war rather than beside it: by 1975 the Palestinian refugees in Lebanon numbered more than 300,000 and the PLO had in effect created a state within a state in the south, which then played an important role in the civil war; and from 1976 Israel was already arming Lebanese Christian militias against the PLO, with the Maronite Phalange under Bashir Gemayel as its main partner. The war aims of June 1982 — destroy the PLO in Lebanon and install a pro-Israel Maronite government under Gemayel — are aims only the civil war made available. The claim is enabling and not causation: the article gives the attempted assassination of Shlomo Argov as the casus belli, and the civil war as what made an invasion of this shape possible.
explanations.lebanese-civil-war--2006-lebanon-war--pr: The war of 2006 was fought between Israel and a party-militia that the civil war produced and that the settlement ending it left armed. Hezbollah was formed during the Israeli invasion and occupation of the south from 1982, and the Taif agreement of 1989, which disarmed the other militias, exempted the resistance to the occupation; when Israel withdrew in 2000 the exemption stayed. That is why in July 2006 the state of Lebanon was not the belligerent and could not restrain the one that was. The claim is about that inheritance, not about the raid that started the fighting.
explanations.legislative-election-1976--eec-applicati: The application was made by a government with an elected parliament behind it, and that was much of its point: Portugal applied as a working parliamentary democracy, which it had only been since the April election. A provisional government could not have applied on those terms.
explanations.lisbon-regicide--1908-portuguese-legisla: João Franco’s government fell within days of the killing, and with it the rule by decree that had suspended parliament since May 1907. The election of 5 April 1908 was the instrument by which the new king’s ministers returned the country to constitutional forms. Without the regicide there is no reason to think the country would have been consulted at all: Franco had dissolved the Chamber precisely in order not to consult it.
explanations.lisbon-regicide--republic-proclaimed-191: The killing took away the king who had backed the dictatorship and the heir who had been trained to succeed him, and left the throne to an eighteen-year-old with no standing of his own. What the monarchy lost was not a battle but the capacity to have one fought for it: its defenders spent the next thirty-two months in ministries too short-lived to govern, while the republican movement had been shown that the regime could be struck at directly and survived the striking. The revolution of October 1910 was made against a dynasty that had already been broken in the Terreiro do Paço.
explanations.maastricht-treaty--amsterdam-treaty--pre: Amsterdam is an amendment to Maastricht and was provided for by it: Maastricht wrote a review conference into its own text, and the intergovernmental conference that produced the treaty of October 1997 is that review. What it amended is the thing Portugal had ratified in 1992 and was inside. The claim is the plain institutional one and it is worth having because it is the spine the next two records hang from.
explanations.maastricht-treaty--euro-adoption-1999--p: The criteria Portugal spent the 1990s meeting are in the treaty: a deficit under three per cent, debt under sixty or falling towards it, inflation and long rates within a margin of the best three, and two years in the exchange rate mechanism. Portugal was in the first group of eleven on 1 January 1999 because it had met them, and the meeting of them is what Portuguese fiscal policy after 1992 consisted of. The treaty also decided what kind of union it would be — a single monetary policy with no common budget and no lender of last resort for governments — which is the design that made the fall in interest rates after 1999 arrive without any brake on what it financed.
explanations.march-on-rome--beer-hall-putsch--inspire: Munich in November 1923 was an attempt to do what Rome had done thirteen months earlier, and its organisers said so. The plan was to seize Bavaria and march on Berlin as Mussolini had marched on Rome; the failure taught the lesson the party then acted on for ten years, which was that power had to be arrived at rather than seized. The claim is about the model and the intention, not about the outcome, which was the opposite of the Italian one.
explanations.march-on-rome--constitution-1933--inspir: The corporative state the constitution of 1933 set up was built on a model Italy had made, and the model is the whole of what this edge claims. The National Assembly with a single party in it, the Corporative Chamber beside it, the labour statute and the strike ban, the vocabulary of the organic nation against the party state: Salazar read the Italian arrangements and his collaborators studied them, and the Portuguese text of 1933 is unintelligible without them. The claim is about the shape of the institutions and is marked probable for a reason the Portuguese historiography insists on: Salazar was not Mussolini, the Estado Novo demobilised where fascism mobilised, and the constitution of 1933 borrowed the corporative machinery precisely in order to have the thing without the movement. Inspired is the right type here and caused would be wrong.
explanations.march-on-rome--lateran-treaty--precondit: The English article on the treaty names the parties: agreements "between Italy under King Victor Emmanuel III and Duce Benito Mussolini and the Holy See under Pope Pius XI to settle the long-standing Roman question". The article on the march says it is what put Mussolini there — the demonstration of October 1922 "resulted in Benito Mussolini’s National Fascist Party ascending to power in the Kingdom of Italy", the King appointing him Prime Minister on 30 October. The Roman question is older than either; what the march supplies is the government that settled it.
explanations.molotov-ribbentrop-pact--german-soviet-t: The English article opens by calling the treaty "a second supplementary protocol of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact of 23 August 1939", amended on 28 September 1939 after the joint German and Soviet invasion and occupation of Poland, superseding the first treaty. Its secret articles redrew parts of the spheres of interest the pact had dictated and moved Lithuania into the Soviet sphere to compensate for Polish territory the Wehrmacht had taken. There is no treaty of 28 September without the pact it supplements.
explanations.molotov-ribbentrop-pact--katyn-massacre-: The prisoners shot in April and May 1940 were taken in September 1939, when the Soviet Union occupied eastern Poland — the half the pact's secret protocol of 23 August had assigned it. Without that protocol there is no Soviet advance into Poland that autumn, and without the advance the NKVD is not holding twenty-two thousand Polish officers, policemen and officials to shoot. The edge is `enabled` rather than `caused` because the pact says nothing about what to do with prisoners: the order of March 1940 was Stalin's and Beria's, and the reasoning behind it — removing the officer class of a state the two signatories had agreed to abolish — belongs to Soviet policy and not to the treaty. What the treaty did was put those men in Soviet hands, which is the sense in which it is a condition of the massacre and not its cause.
explanations.molotov-ribbentrop-pact--winter-war--ena: The secret protocol of 23 August 1939 put Finland in the Soviet sphere, and that is what made the demands of October and the invasion of 30 November possible without a European war following. Germany, which had been the counterweight in the Baltic, was bound not to object and did not; Britain and France were at war with Germany and could reach Finland only through neutral Scandinavia. The claim is about the diplomatic freedom the pact bought, not about the Soviet motive, which was the security of Leningrad and was older than the pact.
explanations.molotov-ribbentrop-pact--world-war-ii--e: Hitler had decided on Poland before he had the pact, and the British guarantee of March 1939 meant the attack risked a general war. What Moscow supplied on 23 August was the removal of the second front: a Germany not fighting the Soviet Union could fight in the west, and the secret protocol gave Stalin a price for staying out. Poland was attacked nine days later. The claim is about the timing and the confidence of the decision, not that the pact caused the war — the demand on Danzig and the corridor was already made, and Britain and France had already committed themselves.
explanations.monarchy-of-the-north-1919--coup-28-may-: On one reading the failure of 1919 settled the question of method for the Republic's enemies: a dynastic restoration by arms could not be had, and what remained was a military intervention that left the form of the state alone — which is what 1926 was.
explanations.moscow-peace-treaty--continuation-war--p: The English article on the Continuation War says the Soviet Union and Finland had previously fought the Winter War, which ended with the Moscow Peace Treaty, and that numerous reasons have been proposed for the Finnish decision to invade, with regaining territory lost during the Winter War regarded as the most common. The article names other proposed motives beside it — Ryti's Greater Finland and Mannerheim's wish to annex East Karelia — so the treaty is where the article starts and not the whole of what it says decided the war.
explanations.mozambique-war-begins-1964--1977-mozambi: The war that opened at Chai in September 1964 is what made FRELIMO the government of Mozambique. It fought the Portuguese state for ten years; it was recognised at Lusaka in 1974 as the only party Lisbon would negotiate the transfer with, without a ballot being held to establish that; and it took the state whole at independence in June 1975. The election of 1977 is that state asking to be confirmed by a single list. The monopoly on the paper is the war's monopoly on the nationalist movement carried into government — which is also why the atlas can wire this ballot at all, where it retracted the colonial elections of the same country before 1974.
explanations.mozambique-war-begins-1964--wiriyamu-mas: Eight years of counter-insurgency in the Tete district — the strategic hamlets, the free-fire reasoning, the pressure to show results against a movement that had reached the Zambezi — are the conditions in which the killings happened. The war does not explain the order; it explains the situation the order was given in.
explanations.mueda-massacre--mozambique-war-begins-19: The argument is the one FRELIMO itself made and most accounts of the war repeat: Mueda ended the case for petitioning. The Makonde cooperative movement had gone to the administration with a demand and had been shot at for it, and the men who founded the nationalist parties out of which FRELIMO was assembled in 1962 came from that milieu. What the edge does not claim is a straight line — the movement was built in Tanganyika out of three exile parties, on the Cold War's terms as much as on Mueda's — and the toll is disputed. What is not disputed is that after 1960 nobody in the north argued for petitioning again.
explanations.munich-agreement--first-vienna-award--ca: The English article's second sentence says the arbitration and the award were direct consequences of the previous month's Munich Agreement, which resulted in the partitioning of Czechoslovakia. The award separated from Czechoslovakia the mostly Hungarian-populated territories of southern Slovakia and southern Carpathian Rus' and returned them to Hungary.
explanations.munich-agreement--molotov-ribbentrop-pac: The Soviet Union had a treaty with Czechoslovakia and was not invited to Munich, and the lesson Moscow drew — that Britain and France would neither fight for eastern Europe nor treat the Soviet Union as a partner in defending it — is the standard explanation for why the collective-security policy of Litvinov was abandoned for Molotov's search for an accommodation with Berlin in 1939. The claim is that Munich made the pact thinkable, not that it made it necessary: the Anglo-French mission to Moscow in the summer of 1939 was also badly handled, and the secret protocol's territorial gains were an inducement Britain could not match.
explanations.nationalisations-1975--25-november-1975-: The nationalisations and the agrarian occupations of 1975 radicalised the revolutionary process; the moderate military and the parties that acted on 25 November were reacting against that course.
explanations.nationalisations-1975--edp-created-1976-: The company of 1976 is made out of what the nationalisations took. March 1975 is where this atlas puts the wave — the banks first, insurance the next day — and because the banks held much of Portuguese industry, what followed them into public ownership over that year included the electricity concerns. EDP is the state deciding what to do with them. The claim is that the expropriation is the precondition of the merger and not that it required it: a state can own fourteen companies and leave them fourteen, and the choice of a single vertically integrated monopoly was a choice, made by a government of 1976 and not by the Council of the Revolution of 1975. The decree that constituted it is not cited here because this run could not point at it in a source it has read.
explanations.nationalisations-1975--imf-agreement-197: One account traces the payments crisis to the revolutionary period itself: the nationalised sector's losses, the wage rises, the collapse of investment and the loss of colonial trade left a deficit that no Portuguese government could finance, and the Fund's terms followed from that.
explanations.nato-founding-1949--un-admission-1955--e: Membership of the Atlantic alliance placed Portugal firmly in the Western camp and is argued to have secured Western sponsorship of its admission to the United Nations.
explanations.noite-sangrenta-1921--coup-28-may-1926--: The murders of October 1921 fixed the Republic's association with political violence in conservative and military opinion, and were still invoked in 1926 as evidence that the regime could not keep order.
explanations.october-revolution--finnish-civil-war--p: The Bolshevik seizure of power is the nearer of the two preconditions the atlas now holds. It removed the Provisional Government with which the Finnish parliament had been quarrelling over sovereignty, it produced the recognition of Finnish independence on 31 December 1917, and it gave the Finnish Social Democrats both an example of what a seizure of power looked like and a neighbour who would arm them. The claim stops there. The Finnish split was Finnish, made by the crisis over the Power Act and the food shortage, and Petrograd neither ordered the rising nor saved it.
explanations.october-revolution--russian-civil-war--c: The seizure of power in Petrograd was cheap and the country it claimed was not. Officers of the old army, the socialist parties expelled from the soviets, the Cossack hosts, the nationalities of the borderlands and eventually fourteen intervening foreign powers all refused the new government, and the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly in January 1918 removed the one authority in whose name they might have been reconciled. Historians differ over whether to date the civil war from October, from the spring of 1918 or from the Czechoslovak Legion's revolt in May; none of them separates it from October.
explanations.october-revolution--treaty-of-brest-lito: Peace was the first of the three words the Bolsheviks took power on, and the Decree on Peace was passed by the Congress of Soviets the day after the Winter Palace fell. The government that signed at Brest-Litovsk in March 1918 signed because it had promised to and because it had no army left to refuse with: Trotsky's attempt to leave the war without signing collapsed when the Germans resumed their advance in February. No government of the old regime, and no Provisional Government, would have conceded Poland, the Baltic, Ukraine and Finland.
explanations.ogaden-war--somali-civil-war--caused: The English article ends its lead with the consequence: "The war left Somalia with a disorganized and demoralized army as well as a heavy disapproval from its population. These conditions led to a revolt in the army which eventually spiraled into the ongoing Somali Civil War." The defeat of March 1978, in which almost a third of the regular army and half the air force were lost, is what the article says produced the revolt.
explanations.paris-peace-conference--treaty-of-triano: The Hungarian frontiers were drawn in Paris and they were not drawn on the principle the conference had announced. Self-determination governed where it suited the Allies' new clients, and strategic and economic claims — a railway, a defensible line, a river — governed where it did not, which is how compact Hungarian-speaking districts ended up inside Romania and Czechoslovakia. Hungary, like Germany, was excluded from the negotiation and handed the text, so the settlement arrived with no domestic consent behind it. The grievance the treaty is remembered for is a product of that method.
explanations.paris-peace-conference--treaty-of-versai: The shape of the German treaty follows from how the conference was run rather than from anything agreed in advance. Because Germany was excluded from the negotiation and handed the text, the terms had no German signature of consent behind them and could be called a Diktat from the first day; because the Four could not agree a reparations figure, they wrote a liability clause and left the sum to a commission, which is the arrangement that kept the question open for a decade; and because Wilson traded points to keep the League in the treaty, the League arrived attached to terms that the United States Senate then refused. The conference did not merely produce the treaty: it produced the treaty's particular defects.
explanations.partition-of-india--indo-pakistani-war-o: The English article says the war was the first of the India–Pakistan wars between the two newly independent nations, both dominions within the British Commonwealth, and that Pakistan precipitated it a few weeks after its independence by launching tribal militias from Waziristan to capture Kashmir and pre-empt the possibility of its ruler joining India. The princely state's choice was open because the partition had released the states from their obligations to the British.
explanations.partition-of-india--kashmir-conflict--ca: The English article on the Kashmir conflict says it started after the partition of India in 1947, as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, and that the dispute escalated into three wars between the two states and several other armed skirmishes. The article on the partition says it divided British India into the two dominions at midnight on 14–15 August 1947 and ended Crown rule in India.
explanations.petrobras-1953--operation-car-wash-2014-: The scheme the investigation found was a scheme inside state companies, and the largest amounts of bribes by far were detected at Petrobras: directors negotiated with contractors for kickbacks, part of which went to the parties. A state oil monopoly is not a cause of corruption, and this edge does not say it is. It says that the thing Lava Jato investigated is the company Law 2,004 created, and that sixty-one years is the distance between the two records.
explanations.petrobras-1953--the-base-reforms-rally-1: One of the three decrees Goulart announced from the platform at the Central do Brasil expropriated the remaining private refineries in favour of Petrobras. The company created in 1953 is what that decree expanded and what it expanded into; without the monopoly of 1953 there is nothing for the refineries to be expropriated in favour of.
explanations.petrobras-1953--the-commodity-boom-and-t: Oil is one of the commodities the fourth buyer came for, and the company that produces it is the one the monopoly of 1953 created: Chinese investment in Brazil has gone into financing oil exploration as well as repairing railways, and Petrobras is what there was to invest in. `enabled` and not `caused`: the boom was made by demand from emerging markets and above all from China, and what the state monopoly supplied was a Brazilian counterparty large enough to sell at that scale.
explanations.pimenta-de-castro-government-1915--revol: The revolt was made against this government and ended with it: the suspension of parliament, the rule by decree and the readmission of monarchists to public life are what the insurgents named as their reasons, and they stopped fighting once the government fell.
explanations.platt-amendment-1901--cuban-revolution--: Three statements, each from its own source, and the edge is what they amount to together. The Amendment gave the United States the absolute right to involve itself in Cuban affairs and leases for naval stations, written word for word into the Cuban constitution. What followed its acceptance was a reciprocity tariff giving Cuban sugar preference in the American market, and American investment on a scale that concentrated a fifth of all Cuban land into the largest mills — the cited account puts the further impoverishment of the rural masses, the constant fear of eviction, the cheap imported labour and the wages held down beside it. And in the decades after 1898 and the formal independence of 20 May 1902, Cuba went through revolts, coups, an American military occupation and an intervention in 1906, in a republic whose politics the same account calls a route to private wealth. The edge does not say the Amendment produced Batista. It says the republic the revolution overthrew was constituted with another state’s right of entry inside it and its land inside another state’s market.
explanations.polish-soviet-war--peace-of-riga--caused: The English article's first sentence says the treaty was signed in Riga on 18 March 1921 between Poland on one side and Soviet Russia and Soviet Ukraine on the other, ending the Polish–Soviet War of 1919 to 1921. What the treaty then settled — a border some 250 kilometres east of the Curzon Line, and Poland's recognition of Soviet Ukraine and Belarus — the article reports as its terms and not as the war's outcome by itself.
explanations.portugal-backs-franco-1936--iberian-pact: Salazar’s support for the Nationalists — the transit of arms and men, the Viriatos, non-intervention as practised rather than as written — was not sentiment about a fellow authoritarian. What he wanted out of a Nationalist victory was a neighbour that owed Portugal something and had no designs on it, and the treaty signed in Lisbon a fortnight before the war ended, by the victor’s own brother, recognising the frontier and promising consultation, is close to being that want written down.
explanations.portugal-backs-franco-1936--legiao-portu: The Legion was created in the months when the government was committing itself against the Spanish Republic, and was justified in exactly those terms: an armed civilian body against the communist danger that the war next door was said to demonstrate.
explanations.portugal-backs-franco-1936--spanish-civi: Salazar's government did not have a Spanish policy before July 1936 and improvised one in a fortnight, out of the belief that a Popular Front victory next door would not stop at the border. Everything it then did — the frontier left open to the rebels, Radio Club Português put at their disposal, republican refugees returned to be shot, the Viriatos allowed to enlist, and the seat on the Non-Intervention Committee taken in order to be obstructive from inside — is a response to the war rather than a policy the war interrupted. The atlas keeps the direction of that dependence explicit because the Estado Novo later preferred to tell it the other way round.
explanations.portugal-e-o-futuro-1974--carnation-revo: The book gave the captains' movement a political horizon and a senior general willing to lead; its publication and the regime's reaction to it are the immediate political context of the conspiracy that acted on 25 April.
explanations.portuguese-colonial-war-1961-1974--carna: The English article on the revolution says the coup of 25 April 1974 came in the midst of the Portuguese Colonial War in the overseas colonies, that it was organised by the Armed Forces Movement of officers who opposed the regime, and that it resulted in an end to that war. The article on the war says the same from its own end: the Estado Novo was overthrown by a military coup in 1974 and the change of government brought the conflict to an end. Both articles put the war and the coup in one another’s account without either calling the war the cause, which is why this is drawn as a precondition and as probable.
explanations.potsdam-conference--nato-founding-1949--: Potsdam left Germany divided into zones under four administrations with no agreed future, and the four years that followed — the failure of the councils of foreign ministers, the currency reform, the Berlin blockade — turned the provisional line into a frontier. The Atlantic treaty of April 1949 is the western answer to that, and it is the door through which Portugal, a dictatorship that had spent the war neutral and had been kept out of the United Nations, entered the western system as a founder member. The claim is about the sequence from a deferred German question to a standing alliance, not that Potsdam was intended to produce one.
explanations.profit-remittance-law-1962--operation-br: The reading this edge states: what turned Washington from pressure to removal was what Brazil was doing to foreign capital. Wikipedia’s account of the deterioration in relations names the Profit Remittance Act first among the factors, alongside the expropriations of American companies by Brizola, the nationalisation of an ITT subsidiary, the difficulty of American credits, and economic reasons. The law capped remittance of profits on foreign capital at ten per cent a year, and on Wikipedia’s account it changed the accounting of the large foreign companies outright. Marxist scholarship of the 1960s and 1970s placed heavy emphasis on the American factor, and Dreifuss’s 1964: A Conquista do Estado (1981) reads the coup as the project of entrepreneurs linked to international capital who concluded that to secure their interests they would have to conquer the state. On this reading Brother Sam is what a threatened buyer does about its supplier.
explanations.profit-remittance-law-1962--the-base-ref: The law of 1962 is the fiscal limb of the base reforms, and the rally of 13 March 1964 is where the reforms stopped being a programme and became decrees. Wikipedia’s account of the reforms puts the cap on profit remittance under the fiscal reform and the decree regulating it, 53,451, in 1964 — the same season as the rally.
explanations.republic-proclaimed-1910--1911-portugues: The Provisional Government installed on 5 October 1910 held power without any title anyone had voted for, and said from the first day that it would call a constituent assembly to give the new regime a constitution. The election of 28 May 1911 was that promise kept. It is the revolution’s own instrument, not an event that would have happened without it.
explanations.republic-proclaimed-1910--constitution-1: The revolution created the Constituent Assembly whose task was to replace the monarchical Charter; the 1911 constitution is the direct institutional product of 5 October.
explanations.republic-proclaimed-1910--first-portugue: The English article on the First Republic bounds it by the two events: it spans the sixteen years between the end of the constitutional monarchy marked by the 5 October 1910 revolution and the 28 May 1926 coup d’état.
explanations.republic-proclaimed-1910--law-of-separat: Anticlericalism was central to the republican programme before 1910, and the provisional government legislated against the Church within weeks of taking power; the Law of Separation was the culmination of that programme rather than a later departure from it.
explanations.republic-proclaimed-1910--universities-o: The provisional government legislated by decree from October 1910 and this is one of its decrees, made in the first six months, alongside the divorce law, the separation of church and state and the reform of primary schooling. The claim is about the programme and its authorship, not about inevitability: republicanism in Portugal had been an educational movement as much as a political one, its strength was in the professional schools of Lisbon and Porto that the decree turned into universities, and the men who signed it had taught in them. A monarchy that had survived 1910 would very likely have founded them too, later and differently; what October 1910 decided was that it was done at once and by these people.
explanations.revolt-14-may-1915--1915-portuguese-legi: Pimenta de Castro had governed with the Chamber suspended; the rising of 14 May removed him and the question of a parliament was open again at once. The election of 13 June followed directly from the overthrow, and returned the party that had made it.
explanations.revolt-14-may-1915--sidonio-pais-coup-19: The victory of May 1915 restored Democratic dominance by force and taught both sides that the way out of a parliamentary defeat was a rising. Sidónio's coup two and a half years later was made against exactly the dominance that May restored, and by men who had learned the same lesson.
explanations.revolutions-of-1989--dissolution-of-the-: The English article on the revolutions says they were a wave of liberal democratic movements that resulted in the collapse of most Marxist–Leninist governments in the Eastern Bloc, and that they were a key factor in the dissolution of the Soviet Union and in the abandonment of communist regimes in many parts of the world. "A key factor" is the article’s own weighting, and is why this is drawn as probable.
explanations.revolutions-of-1989--maastricht-treaty--: The English article on the treaty says it was negotiated against the background of the end of the Cold War and the re-unification of Germany, and in anticipation of accelerated globalisation, between member states seeking deeper integration and those wishing to retain greater national control. The article on the revolutions of 1989 says it is they that marked the end of the Cold War and the beginning of the post–Cold War era. Neither article says the revolutions produced the treaty, which is why this is a precondition and not a cause.
explanations.revolutions-of-1989--romanian-revolution: The English article on the revolutions of 1989 describes a wave of liberal democratic movements that collapsed most Marxist–Leninist governments in the Eastern Bloc, some of which were violently overthrown. December 1989 in Romania is one of that wave, and its own retraction said it could not be argued from anything else because the atlas held none of the others.
explanations.russian-civil-war--kronstadt-rebellion--: The English article puts the rising inside the war and gives war communism as what produced it: as the civil war wound down in late 1920 the Bolsheviks faced "mass disillusionment from unbearable living conditions—famine, disease, cold, and weariness—induced by the years of war and exacerbated by the Bolshevik policy of war communism", peasants resented the requisitioning of grain, bread rations in the cities were cut by a third in January 1921, and the Cheka reported 155 peasant risings in February. The article calls Kronstadt the last major revolt against Bolshevik rule on Russian territory during the civil war.
explanations.russian-revolution-of-1905--constitution: Persia watched 1905 from next door and read it as an instruction. Russia was the power that had lent to the Qajar shahs against the customs revenue and garrisoned the Cossack Brigade that guarded them, and the sight of an autocracy conceding a duma to strikes and street protest was the news that mattered to the bazaaris, the clergy and the intellectuals who took sanctuary in Tehran in the summer of 1906 and got a constitution out of it. Persians working in the Caucasus oil fields carried the politics home. The claim is about the example; the Persian grievances, the tobacco concession and the debt and the customs administration, were Persian.
explanations.russian-revolution-of-1905--february-rev: February 1917 repeated 1905 in its form — a strike in the capital, the garrison refusing to fire, a council of workers' and soldiers' deputies constituting itself beside the official assembly — because the institutions and the people were the ones 1905 had made. The soviet was a device invented in St Petersburg twelve years earlier; the parties that filled it had been legalised, and then harassed, under the constitution 1905 extracted. The claim is about the repertoire and the personnel, not that 1905 made 1917 inevitable.
explanations.russian-revolution-of-1905--treaty-of-po: Russia opened negotiations at Portsmouth in August 1905 with the revolution seven months old, the Black Sea fleet mutinying and the countryside burning, and accepted terms — Korea, the Liaodong lease, southern Sakhalin — that a government secure at home would have gone on fighting rather than sign. The claim is that the revolution is why Russia settled in 1905 rather than in 1906, not that it is why Russia lost: Japan was near the end of its credit and Roosevelt was pressing both sides, and either would have brought the war to an end in time.
explanations.russo-japanese-war--british-russian-conv: The English article says that the emergence of the German Empire as a world power and **the defeat in 1905 of Russia by a nascent Asian power, the Empire of Japan, in the Russo-Japanese War**, helped to persuade some British and Russian officials of a need to resolve their respective differences in Asia — the differences over Afghanistan, Iran and Tibet that the convention settled. The defeat is one of the two reasons the article gives for a bargain both sides had resisted for twenty years.
explanations.russo-japanese-war--russian-revolution-o: The article says that Russia’s incurrence of substantial casualties and losses for a cause which resulted in a humiliating defeat contributed to internal unrest culminating in the 1905 Russian Revolution, during which the Russian autocracy was forced to make concessions. The word the article uses is "contributed to", which is why this is drawn as probable and not as consensus.
explanations.salazar-finance-minister-1928--salazar-p: The balanced budgets from 1928 onwards were the basis of Salazar's authority within the dictatorship; his political ascendancy over the military was built on his financial record.
explanations.salazar-president-of-council-1932--const: Salazar used the head of government's position to draft and impose the constitution that institutionalised his power; the 1933 text is his regime's founding act.
explanations.santa-maria-hijacking-1961--angola-war-b: The hijacking drew the international press to Portugal and its empire, and several accounts hold that the Luanda attacks of early February were timed to strike while that attention was still on Lisbon, giving them a hearing they would not otherwise have had.
explanations.schengen-agreement--schengen-in-force-19: What Portugal joined in 1991 and applied in 1995 was not a Community policy but the club of 1985, and the shape of that club decides both halves of what Portugal got. Because Schengen was built outside the treaties, accession to it was a separate act that Portugal and Spain could take together five years after joining the Communities, rather than something that came with membership. And because the 1990 convention paid for open internal borders with a common external one, the abolition of checks on the Spanish frontier arrived bound to the obligation to hold the Atlantic coast and the airports on everyone else's behalf — which is where the Portuguese argument about Schengen has been ever since.
explanations.second-balkan-war--assassination-of-arch: The second war left Serbia larger again and Bulgaria hostile, and it is the point at which Vienna concluded that the Serbian problem would have to be settled rather than managed. The Austro-Hungarian general staff had asked for a preventive war against Serbia repeatedly since 1908 and been refused; what the summer of 1913 changed was the answer, not the question. This is the more immediate of the two Balkan preconditions the atlas now holds, and it is marked probable because the counterfactual is genuinely open: Vienna might have been refused once more.
explanations.second-sino-japanese-war--chinese-civil-: The two Chinese parties had been at war with each other before Japan attacked and suspended it for the united front; the question is what eight years of Japanese war did to their relative strength. It destroyed the Nationalists' German-trained divisions in the first year, drove their government to the interior, and left it holding a ruined tax base and a currency that collapsed in 1947–48; the Communist bases in the north, fighting a guerrilla war behind the Japanese lines, came out of it with a mass organisation and a territory. The claim is about that reversal, not that Japan chose the winner.
explanations.second-sino-japanese-war--tripartite-pac: Japan signed in Berlin in September 1940 because it had been at war in China for three years and could not finish it. The war had brought the American embargoes and the aid to Chongqing, it had made the resources of South-East Asia look like the way out, and an alliance that might deter the United States from intervening was worth having for both reasons. The claim is about the Japanese motive for the pact and not about the German or Italian ones, which were different.
explanations.second-sudanese-civil-war--2011-south-su: The English article on the war says it ran from 1983 to 2005 between the central Sudanese government and the Sudan People's Liberation Army, and that the war resulted in the independence of South Sudan six years after it ended. The English article on the referendum says the vote was one of the consequences of the 2005 Naivasha Agreement between the Khartoum government and the SPLA/M. Both are the encyclopedia, so this link rests on one author.
explanations.second-sudanese-civil-war--war-in-darfur: The English article gives several different explanations for the origins of the conflict that started in 2003 — land disputes between semi-nomadic herders and sedentary farmers, access to water, and the two rebel groups against the Khartoum government — and among them says the Darfur crisis is also related to the First and Second Sudanese civil wars between the Arab-dominated government and the Christian and animist black southerners. The article relates them and does not rank them: this link is one of several the page offers and is written at the strength the page gives it.
explanations.sidonio-pais-assassinated-1918--1918-por: The English article says the election was held two days after the assassination of President Sidónio Pais on 14 December 1918, that quorum was not reached at the first ballot so it was repeated with the necessary members present, and that João do Canto e Castro was elected as the new President succeeding the late Sidónio Pais. The vacancy is what the article gives as the occasion; what followed from it politically is not this edge.
explanations.sidonio-pais-assassinated-1918--monarchy: The killing of Sidónio removed the one figure around whom the anti-Democratic right had gathered and left it without a route to power through the Republic. The monarchist rising followed within five weeks, into that vacuum and with officers who had served the New Republic.
explanations.sidonio-pais-assassinated-1918--noite-sa: The assassination reopened the cycle of coups and counter-coups; the violence of October 1921 belongs to the sequence of instability that began with the collapse of the República Nova.
explanations.single-european-act--maastricht-treaty--: The English article says that, anticipating the 1992 Maastricht Treaty, the Act's signatories declared themselves moved by the will to continue the work undertaken on the basis of the treaties establishing the European Communities and to transform relations as a whole among their states into a European Union. The article also calls the Act a forerunner of the Union's Common Foreign and Security Policy, which Maastricht is where that became a pillar.
explanations.sino-indian-war--indo-pakistani-war-of-1: The English article on the war of 1965 gives the defeat of 1962 as part of what made Pakistan think the moment had come: after its success in the Rann of Kutch, Pakistan under Ayub Khan "believed the Indian Army would be unable to defend itself against a quick military campaign in the disputed territory of Kashmir as the Indian military had suffered a loss to China in 1962 in the Sino-Indian War". The claim is about a belief the article attributes to the Pakistani leadership, which is why the type is `enabled` and the confidence `probable`.
explanations.soviet-afghan-war--dissolution-of-the-so: The English article says the decade-long confrontation between the mujahideen and the Soviet and Afghan militaries inflicted grave destruction throughout Afghanistan and has been cited by scholars as a significant factor contributing to the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, which is why the conflict is sometimes called the Soviet Union's Vietnam. The article reports that as what scholars have said and puts the war among the factors, not as the cause.
explanations.soviet-afghan-war--war-in-afghanistan-20: The English article says the war of 2001 was part of the ongoing Afghan conflict rather than a thing on its own, and that the force it was fought against carried the earlier war forward: "Owing to their roots in the anti-Soviet mujahideen, the Taliban carried on the guerrilla tactics developed in the 1980s." The cause the article gives for the invasion is the attacks of 11 September 2001, which this atlas does not hold; what is claimed here is only the precondition the article states, that the adversary of 2001 came out of the war of the 1980s.
explanations.spanish-civil-war--iberian-pact--caused: The pact of 17 March 1939 was signed a fortnight before the war formally ended and with its outcome settled, and the thing it settled was the danger the war had created for Lisbon: a Spain under a victorious military regime, indebted to Berlin and Rome, on the only land frontier Portugal has. The atlas already holds the argument that Portugal's own support for the Nationalists earned it the pact. This edge makes the other half of the claim — that what Salazar wanted from the pact was a Spain bound to stay out of a European war, which is what the Iberian bloc turned out to be worth in 1940.
explanations.spinola-resigns-1974--coup-attempt-11-ma: Having lost the presidency in September, Spínola and the officers around him had no institutional route back; what they attempted in March was the attempt of men already outside. The resignation is what put them there.
explanations.the-1930-revolution-and-the-vargas-era--: The republic the coup overthrew was Vargas’s residue. The Fourth Republic began in 1946 with his ousting; all three of its major parties came out of him — the PTB carrying his labour legacy, the PSD grown from his political machine, the UDN from the opposition to him — and the opposition between national-statists and liberal-conservatives that the sources say organised the whole period is the argument about his settlement. The crises that preceded 1964, in 1954, 1955 and 1961, are the same two blocs failing to remove each other. `precondition-of` and not `caused`: 1930 did not require 1964, and the thirty-four years between them contain their own decisions.

The company was created by decree of Getúlio Vargas during the Estado Novo, its shares authorised by decree-laws of January and April 1941, and Vargas greeted it in 1943 as the symbol of Brazil’s economic emancipation. A state steelworks financed abroad is the Estado Novo’s own instrument and not something that happened during it.

The men were conscripted, not recruited. The Estado Novo ordered compulsory enlistment in 1943 through SEMTA, based at Fortaleza, and created SAVA, SESP, SNAPP and the Rubber Credit Bank around it; Vargas, on Wikipedia’s account, reduced the problem of a drought-stricken Northeast and increased the settlement of the Amazon at the same time. Thousands were transported under force to obligatory servitude and about thirty thousand died there.

Somebody had to say yes. Brazil broke off relations with Germany, Japan and Italy in January 1942 in exchange for direct American economic assistance and allowed the bases to be built; the alignment was the Estado Novo’s decision, taken against a government whose own sympathies had been read both ways, and it cost Brazil thirty-six merchant ships and two thousand lives before the year was out.
explanations.the-1988-brazilian-constitution--the-imp: The charges were laid under article 85, items V and VI, of the constitution of 1988, and the procedure — acceptance by the president of the Chamber, a vote of the Chamber, suspension, trial in the Senate — is the one that text lays down. The instrument that removed a president in 2016 is the one written to replace a regime that had removed them by other means.
explanations.the-base-reforms-rally-1964--1964-brazil: On Wikipedia’s account the rally of the 13th and the message to Congress of the 15th marked the end of conciliation: the president had opted for confrontation at the end of February and meant to hold rallies until a general strike on 1 May. The opposition answered in kind — Ademar de Barros demanding impeachment on the 15th, the March of the Family with God for Liberty on the 20th, the sailors’ revolt on the 25th, the Automóvel Clube on the 30th — and the officers moved on the 31st. `precondition-of` rather than `caused`, deliberately: the conspiracy had been running since 1961 and the men who brought the date forward had reasons of their own, from Guedes’s imminent replacement to Mourão’s compulsory retirement. What the rally supplied was the confrontation, not the decision.
explanations.the-brazilian-debt-crisis-1982--1985-bra: What the regime had to show for twenty-one years by 1983 was an inflation of 239 per cent, and the Diretas Já movement grew alongside it — the first protest at Abreu e Lima on 31 March 1983, then Goiânia, then Pacaembu. The direct election was refused and the electoral college met anyway under no coercion, which is what a regime does when it has lost the argument rather than the vote.
explanations.the-brazilian-miracle-1968-1973--the-bra: The growth was borrowed. To fuel it Brazil needed ever more imported oil, and after the shock of 1973 the military government borrowed increasingly from international lenders until the debt was unmanageable; by the end of the decade it was the largest in the world, about ninety-two billion dollars. Growth ended with the energy crisis of 1979 and gave way to recession and hyperinflation.
explanations.the-end-of-the-amazon-rubber-monopoly--t: This is the sharpest link in the third movement and it runs backwards through thirty years. The Allies lost ninety-seven per cent of Asian rubber production when Japan took Malaya at the beginning of 1942 — and the production was Asian in the first place because seeds taken out of Brazil in 1876 had been planted in British colonies and had undercut the Amazon by 1912. The collapse of the Brazilian monopoly is what put the world’s rubber inside Japan’s reach, and that is what sent the United States back to the Amazon to buy what it had stopped buying.
explanations.the-holocaust--european-convention-on-hu: The convention of 1950 was drafted by governments that had just watched a state destroy its own citizens legally, and it is built against that: rights held by individuals against the state rather than granted by it, a court that a person may reach, and a list — life, torture, slavery, arbitrary detention — that reads as an inventory of what had been done. The claim is about what the drafters were answering, which the preamble and the drafting record say plainly. It is not that the Holocaust alone produced the convention: the Soviet presence in eastern Europe and the wish to bind the new German state are in it too.
explanations.the-holocaust--genocide-convention--caus: The convention of 9 December 1948 was written because of what had been done in Europe between 1941 and 1945, and by a man who had lost his family in it. Lemkin coined the word in 1944 and spent the next four years getting it into a treaty; the General Assembly adopted the convention the day before the Universal Declaration, and the drafting arguments over which groups the definition would cover were arguments about how far the European case generalised. The claim is that the Holocaust is the cause of the instrument; it is not a claim that the instrument worked.
explanations.the-holocaust--porajmos--enabled: The English article says that a supplementary decree to the Nuremberg Laws, issued on 26 November 1935, classified Roma as "enemies of the race-based state", "thereby placing them in the same category as the Jews", and that thus the fate of the Sinti and Roma in Europe paralleled that of the Jews in the Holocaust. What is claimed here is that the racial law and the apparatus built for the persecution this atlas records as the Holocaust were extended to the Roma, and not that one genocide caused the other: the article dates the persecution of Roma from 1933, alongside rather than after.
explanations.the-holocaust--warsaw-ghetto-uprising--r: The English article says the rising was mounted by the Jewish resistance in the ghetto "to oppose Nazi Germany’s final effort to transport the remaining ghetto population to the gas chambers of the Majdanek and Treblinka extermination camps in 1943", and that it followed the Grossaktion Warsaw of the summer of 1942, in which more than a quarter of a million Jews were deported from the ghetto to Treblinka and murdered, after which the remaining Jews began building bunkers and smuggling in weapons. Read in the atlas’s own direction, the arrow runs from the persecution to the rising and the type names what the later event was: the rising reacted to the deportations, and was not caused by them in the sense that a consequence is.
explanations.the-troubles--good-friday-agreement--cau: The English article on the Troubles says the conflict lasted about thirty years from the late 1960s to 1998 and is usually deemed to have ended with the Good Friday Agreement of that year.
explanations.treaty-of-accession-1985--eec-accession-: Membership of the Communities happens by treaty and on the day the treaty says. The signature of 12 June 1985 is what had to exist for 1 January 1986 to mean anything, and between the two dates lay ratification in twelve parliaments, any one of which could have stopped it. The edge is `precondition-of` and not `caused` for exactly that reason: the treaty did not bring the accession about, it made it possible, and what brought it about was nine years of negotiation and twelve ratifications.
explanations.treaty-of-brest-litovsk--battle-of-the-l: The German spring offensives of 1918 were made possible by the end of the eastern war: the armistice of December 1917 and the treaty of March 1918 released some fifty divisions for the west, and Ludendorff spent them on a run of attacks begun before American strength could arrive. Operation Georgette, which fell on the Lys on 9 April, was the second of them. The claim is about why an attack of that weight was available in that sector in that month, not about why the Portuguese 2nd Division broke under it — the state of the division is argued on the Portuguese record and is not settled here.
explanations.treaty-of-brest-litovsk--polish-soviet-w: The English article on the Polish–Soviet war says that after the collapse of the Central Powers and the Armistice of 11 November 1918, Lenin’s Soviet Russia annulled the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk and moved forces westward to reclaim the Ober Ost regions abandoned by the Germans, and that Lenin viewed the newly independent Poland as a critical route for spreading communist revolution into Europe. The treaty is what had put those lands outside Soviet control, and its annulment is where the article begins the war.
explanations.treaty-of-lausanne--montreux-convention-: Montreux is the revision of a regime Lausanne set. The English article says that in 1923 the Treaty of Lausanne had demilitarised the Dardanelles and opened the Straits to unrestricted civilian and military traffic under an International Straits Commission of the League of Nations; that in April 1935 the Turkish government sent a note to the signatories of Lausanne proposing a conference on a new regime, on the ground that the international situation had changed since 1923; and that as its preamble states, the convention replaced the terms of the Lausanne treaty regarding the Straits.
explanations.treaty-of-london--paris-peace-conference: The secret treaty of April 1915 is what Italy brought to Paris and what Paris would not honour. It had promised the Trentino, Trieste, Istria, a part of Dalmatia and a share of the Ottoman and German settlements in exchange for entering the war within a month, and the peace conference set most of it aside in favour of self-determination for the South Slavs. The Italian delegation walked out in April 1919 over Fiume, which the treaty had not even promised. The claim is about the terms of the Italian quarrel at Paris, not about the whole conference, which had many other things to settle.
explanations.treaty-of-paris--treaty-of-rome--precond: The Coal and Steel Community of 1951 is the institution the Community of 1957 was built on top of: the same six states, a High Authority that became a Commission, a Court, an Assembly, and the demonstration that supranational government of one sector could be made to work. Rome extended the method to a customs union after the defeat of the defence community had shown that the political road was closed. The claim is about the institutional lineage. Portugal was in neither and joined the thing they became thirty-five years later, which is where the atlas picks the story up.
explanations.treaty-of-rome--efta-accession-1960--cau: The European Free Trade Association exists because the Common Market did: it was assembled in 1959–60 by the states outside the Six, on a British initiative, as a free trade area in industrial goods without a common tariff, common policies or supranational institutions — that is, as the arrangement the Six had refused. Portugal was in it because it could not be in the other one. The Stockholm Convention's annex G, which let Portugal keep protective tariffs and reduce them on a longer schedule than anybody else, is the measure of the distance, and joining was still the first binding commitment the Estado Novo made to open the economy.
explanations.treaty-of-rome--maastricht-treaty--preco: Maastricht did not found a new organisation beside the old one: it converted the Community established at Rome, keeping the same members, the same Commission, Council and Court, and the whole accumulated body of law. That is why monetary union arrived attached to an existing legal order with an existing court to enforce it, rather than as a treaty between governments that any of them could reinterpret — and why the Portuguese argument of the 1990s was about how much further to go rather than about whether to be in it. The claim is about the institutional continuity, which is what the treaty text and its own name, the Treaty on European Union, make explicit.
explanations.treaty-of-rome--single-european-act--pre: The English article's first sentence is that the Single European Act was the first major revision of the 1957 Treaty of Rome. It amended rather than replaced: the Act set the European Community the objective of a single market by 31 December 1992 and reformed the Community legislative process by introducing the cooperation procedure and extending qualified majority voting.
explanations.treaty-of-sevres--turkish-war-of-indepen: The nationalist movement in Anatolia predates the treaty — the congresses of Erzurum and Sivas met in 1919, against the Greek landing at Smyrna — so the claim is not that Sèvres began the resistance. It is that Sèvres gave it the thing it had lacked: a signed partition, accepted by the sultan's government, that made the movement in Ankara rather than the government in Constantinople the plausible custodian of the Turkish state. From August 1920 the war was fought over whether that document would be applied, and it ended when Lausanne annulled it.
explanations.treaty-of-trianon--first-vienna-award--p: The same article says Hungary sought to reclaim the territories it had lost and to reunite the Hungarian minority across its borders, that Germany and Italy had supported those claims and the revision of the 1920 Treaty of Trianon imposed on Hungary after the First World War, and that the award regained for Hungary some of what it had lost under Trianon. The treaty is what the claim was a claim against.
explanations.treaty-of-versailles--beer-hall-putsch--: The putsch was mounted in the worst month of the German crisis of 1923, and that crisis was a crisis of the treaty: France and Belgium had occupied the Ruhr in January because Germany had defaulted on reparations deliveries, the government answered with passive resistance financed by printing money, and by November the mark had gone. The politics of the Kampfbund were built entirely on the treaty — the stab in the back, the November criminals, the reparations. The claim is about the occasion and the grievance, not that Versailles produced Nazism: the same treaty was also being fulfilled, at the same moment, by governments that survived it.
explanations.treaty-of-versailles--german-polish-decl: The English article says the 1934 declaration "effectively normalised relations between Poland and Germany, which had been strained by border disputes arising from the territorial settlement in the Treaty of Versailles", and that until then Germany had withheld normalisation without first settling the question of the German-Polish border. What the declaration did was set the Versailles border question aside for ten years, so the settlement is what the declaration was about.
explanations.treaty-of-versailles--locarno-treaties--: The English article describes the main treaty as the five western European states pledging to guarantee the inviolability of the borders between Germany and France and between Germany and Belgium as defined in the Treaty of Versailles, and to observe the demilitarised zone of the Rhineland. The article is equally clear about what was left out: there was no guarantee of Germany's eastern border, leaving the path open for Germany to attempt to revise the Versailles treaty and regain territory it had lost in the east.
explanations.treaty-of-versailles--treaty-of-rapallo-: The English article's background says both Germany and Russia were left vulnerable after the end of the First World War: Germany had lost and become diplomatically isolated, and the postwar Treaty of Versailles led to German disarmament and the cession of German territories including all her colonies; Russia, likewise isolated after the Bolshevik revolution, had ceded its western territories at Brest-Litovsk. The article quotes the reading that the policies pursued by the victors, especially France, left no alternative to Germany but to move closer to Russia. The lead adds that the secret military co-operation already scheduled between the two was itself a violation of Versailles.
explanations.treaty-of-versailles--world-war-ii--prec: The oldest reading of the interwar period makes the treaty the cause of the next war: a settlement harsh enough to embitter Germany and to give revisionist politics its programme, but not harsh enough to prevent Germany from acting on it, with the territorial clauses supplying every demand of the 1930s in order — the Rhineland, the Sudetenland, the corridor, Danzig. The atlas records the link because the demands of 1936 to 1939 really were the treaty's clauses read backwards; it records it as disputed because the step from that to causation is exactly what historians divide over.
explanations.treaty-on-the-non-proliferation-of-nucle: The English article defines the prohibition treaty against the one this atlas already had a record of: nuclear weapons, unlike chemical weapons, biological weapons, landmines and cluster munitions, "are not prohibited in a comprehensive and universal manner", because **"the Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) of 1968 contains only partial prohibitions"** and the nuclear-weapon-free zone treaties prohibit them only regionally. The treaty's own preamble cites the slow pace of nuclear disarmament and expresses compliance with the NPT, and its Article 3 requires parties to keep the safeguards built on the NPT model.
explanations.turkish-war-of-independence--treaty-of-l: Lausanne is the only peace of the First World War settlement negotiated with the defeated side rather than presented to it, and the reason is on the battlefield: the Greek army had been driven out of Anatolia in 1922 and Britain would not fight at Chanak to hold the terms of Sèvres. What the treaty conceded — full sovereignty in Anatolia and eastern Thrace, no Armenian state, no Kurdistan, the capitulations abolished — is the nationalist programme, and the compulsory exchange of populations that came with it was the price the victory was settled at.
explanations.un-admission-1955--angola-war-begins-196: Membership exposed Portugal to the United Nations' pressure on non-self-governing territories under Chapter XI of the Charter, which the regime tried to evade by calling the colonies overseas provinces; the diplomatic isolation this produced is part of the context in which the Angolan movements moved to armed struggle.
explanations.vietnam-war--cambodian-vietnamese-war--p: The English article argues the war out of the alliance that preceded it: during the Vietnam War the Vietnamese and Cambodian communists "again had formed an alliance to fight anti-communist regimes in their respective countries", the Vietnamese used Cambodian territory as a transport route and staging area for attacks on South Vietnam, both took power in April 1975 as the war ended, and the Khmer Rouge — fearing a Vietnamese-dominated Indochinese federation — began purging Vietnamese-trained personnel and attacking southern Vietnam in May 1975.
explanations.vietnam-war--laotian-civil-war--precondi: The English article says the Kingdom of Laos was a covert theatre during the Vietnam War, with both sides receiving heavy external support in a proxy war between the Cold War superpowers, that the North Vietnamese Army invaded Laos in 1958 and 1959 to use the east of the country for the Ho Chi Minh trail and as a staging area for offensives into South Vietnam, and that the Pathet Lao emerged victorious in December 1975 following North Vietnam's final victory in April 1975. The war has its own combatants and its own dates and the article does not make it a part of the other.
explanations.vietnam-war--sino-vietnamese-war--precon: The English article's background opens by putting the three wars in one line: just as the First Indochina War, which emerged from the complex situation following the Second World War, and the Vietnam War arose from the indecisive aftermath of political relations, the Third Indochina War again followed the unresolved problems of the earlier wars. The lead gives the immediate occasion as China's stated response to Vietnam's invasion and occupation of Cambodia in 1978, which is a record this atlas does not hold.
explanations.wall-street-crash-of-1929--great-depress: The conventional account runs from the crash to the Depression through confidence: the collapse of share values destroyed household wealth and lending, consumption and investment fell, and the banking failures of 1930–33 followed. The dating is not in question — the slump does begin in the autumn of 1929 in the United States and spreads outward from there — but the causal weight of the crash itself is, which is why this edge is marked as it is rather than left out.
explanations.war-in-bosnia-and-herzegovina--croat-bos: The English article on the Bosnian war says the conflict was initially between Yugoslav Army units in Bosnia, later the VRS, on one side and the ARBiH and the Croat forces of the HVO on the other, and that tensions between Croats and Bosniaks increased throughout late 1992, resulting in the escalation of the Croat–Bosniak war in early 1993. The article on the smaller war calls it a war within a war for that reason: the allies of the first year turned on each other inside it.
