explanations.war-in-bosnia-and-herzegovina--dayton-ag: The English article on the Bosnian war says it ended on 21 November 1995 when the Dayton Accords were initialed, and that its main belligerents were the forces of the government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and those of the breakaway proto-states of Herzeg-Bosnia and Republika Srpska, led and supplied by Croatia and Serbia respectively.
explanations.war-of-attrition--yom-kippur-war--precon: The English article says that after Nasser's death in September 1970 his successor Anwar Sadat continued the ceasefire, focusing on rebuilding the Egyptian army and planning a full-scale attack on the Israeli forces holding the eastern bank of the Suez Canal, and that "these plans would materialize three years later in the Yom Kippur War". The paragraph carries a citation-needed tag dated December 2025, which is why this is probable and no more.
explanations.winter-war--continuation-war--caused: The English article says that numerous reasons have been proposed for the Finnish decision to go to war again in June 1941, and that regaining the territory lost in the Winter War is regarded as the most common of them. It adds that after the Moscow Peace Treaty Finnish public opinion favoured the reconquest of the ceded territory, that the government made national defence its first priority and raised military spending to nearly half of public spending, and that by September 1941 Finland had regained its post-Winter-War concessions in Karelia. The confidence is `probable` because the article itself says the reasons are several and disputed, not one.
explanations.winter-war--moscow-peace-treaty--caused: The English article's lead says the treaty was signed by Finland and the Soviet Union on 12 March 1940 and marked the end of the 105-day Winter War, upon which Finland ceded border areas to the Soviet Union. The article adds that the terms were not reversed after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, which is the treaty's own afterlife and not part of this link.
explanations.world-war-i--arab-revolt--enabled: The revolt is an operation of the war’s Middle Eastern theatre and could not have been anything else. The Hashemites of the Hejaz rose against the Ottoman state because a Britain at war with that state would pay, arm and ship for them, and the correspondence with McMahon that preceded the rising is a wartime bargain struck for a wartime purpose. Without the war there is no subsidy, no landing at Rabegh and no reason to move in 1916 rather than at some other time. The atlas does not yet hold the Sykes-Picot agreement being negotiated in the same months against the same promises, so the argument about what was promised to whom cannot be made here.
explanations.world-war-i--armenian-genocide--enabled: The deportations began in April 1915, five months after the Ottoman entry into the war and three months after the disaster at Sarikamish, and were carried out under wartime emergency powers, in a theatre closed to outside observation, against a population the Committee of Union and Progress had decided to treat as the Russian enemy's fifth column. The claim is that the war supplied the powers, the pretext and the cover, not that it produced the intention: the argument over when the Committee resolved on destruction rather than deportation is not settled by this edge.
explanations.world-war-i--armistice-of-mudros--caused: The English article's background is the war closing on the Ottoman government: the Macedonian front collapsed in September 1918 and Bulgaria sued for peace, leaving Constantinople to be defended against an overland siege without Bulgarian help; Talaat Pasha returned from Berlin and Sofia understanding that the war was no longer winnable, and resigned with his ministry on 13 October; two days after taking office Ahmed Izzet Pasha sent the captured British general Townshend to the Allies to seek terms. The article hangs that account on Fromkin 2009, pages 360 to 373, which is the second author here. It is the war ending, not a policy the Ottomans chose freely.
explanations.world-war-i--basmachi-movement--precondi: The English article puts the movement's origin in the war itself: "The movement's roots lay in the anti-conscription violence of 1916 which erupted when the Russian Empire began to draft Muslims for army service in World War I." The conscription of Central Asian Muslims for a European war is the first thing the article names, before the Bolsheviks and before Kokand.
explanations.world-war-i--easter-rising--enabled: The Rising was timed against the war and not against anything else. The argument inside the Irish Republican Brotherhood for rising in 1916 rather than at some later moment was that England was committed elsewhere and that Germany, being at war with her, could be asked for arms; the Aud sailed with rifles and was scuttled off the Kerry coast three days before Easter Monday. Home Rule had been passed and suspended for the duration, which is the other half of it: the war both removed the constitutional road and supplied the opportunity. This is not a claim that the war caused Irish republicanism, which is much older than the war.
explanations.world-war-i--estonian-war-of-independenc: The English article describes the campaign as "the struggle of the newly established democratic state of Estonia for independence in the aftermath of World War I", fought against the Soviet Russian westward offensive of 1918–1919 and the 1919 aggression of the pro-German Baltische Landeswehr, and concluded in the 1920 Treaty of Tartu. The state that fought it existed because the war had unmade the empire that held the ground.
explanations.world-war-i--february-revolution--caused: The revolution was made of the war's costs and out of its materials. Two and a half years of it had put some fifteen million men through the Russian army and killed or maimed a large part of them; the railways that fed the front stopped feeding Petrograd, and the bread queues of February 1917 were a transport failure before they were anything else. What turned a strike into a revolution was the garrison — reservists and recruits held in the capital for the war and not yet sent to it — refusing to fire and then joining the crowd, which is a specifically wartime fact about who was standing in Petrograd that week. The autocracy's last defenders had also been spent on the war: Nicholas II had taken personal command in 1915 and so owned every defeat after it, and the Duma politicians who took power in March had spent two years arguing that the government was losing the war. This is `caused` and not `precondition-of` because the claim is about February 1917 and not about whether Russia would ever have had a revolution: the grievances were older than the war, and the argument here is that the war supplied the timing, the hunger and the armed men.
explanations.world-war-i--finnish-civil-war--precondi: Finland was a Russian grand duchy in 1914 and an independent state in a civil war by January 1918, and the war is what stands between the two. It broke the Russian state that had governed Finland, it put a garrison of Russian troops on Finnish soil who would sell or hand over their rifles, it turned the food supply of a country that imported its grain into a famine question, and it made a German intervention possible by giving Germany an interest in the Baltic. The claim is that the war is the condition of the Finnish rupture, not that it decided which side would win it.
explanations.world-war-i--german-revolution-of-1918-1: The revolution began in the navy and it began over the war. The High Seas Fleet was ordered out on 24 October 1918 for a battle that could not change the outcome and that the crews understood as being asked to die for the honour of their officers; the mutiny at Wilhelmshaven and Kiel spread through the garrison towns in a week, and the Empire fell on 9 November. Four years of blockade, of casualty lists and of a war the high command had just admitted was lost are the whole of the cause. It is marked probable rather than consensus only because this atlas holds no work of German history to cite.
explanations.world-war-i--germany-declares-war-1916--: Portugal did not choose the war and then find an occasion; the occasion was made by the war it was already on the edge of. Fighting with German colonial forces in southern Angola and northern Mozambique had been going on since 1914, and the requisition of the interned German ships in February 1916 was carried out at Britain's request under the alliance, in a shipping crisis the submarine campaign had created. The declaration of 9 March 1916 is the point at which a European war already two years old took Portugal into it formally. That the belligerence was sought by the Democrats for their own reasons is a further argument, made on the Portuguese record itself.
explanations.world-war-i--sayfo--enabled: The Sayfo was carried out under the cover of the war and by the state that was fighting it. Assyrian and Syriac Christians were killed and deported from south-eastern Anatolia and from Persian Azerbaijan by Ottoman forces and allied Kurdish tribes in the same years, by the same apparatus and on the same reasoning of internal enemy as the Armenian genocide this atlas already holds. What the war supplied was the front line that ran through where these communities lived, the requisitioning, and the suspension of any authority that might have refused. It did not supply the intention, which was the Committee of Union and Progress’s own; that is why this is enabled and not caused.
explanations.world-war-i--treaty-of-neuilly-sur-seine: The English article's first sentence is the whole of the link: the treaty was between the victorious Allies of the First World War on one side and Bulgaria, one of the defeated Central Powers, on the other, and it required Bulgaria to cede various territories. The article files it with the Treaties of Versailles, Saint-Germain, Trianon and Sèvres as one of the series of treaties after the war intended to diminish the military and political strength of the defeated Central Powers.
explanations.world-war-ii--20-july-plot--caused: The plot of July 1944 was made by officers who had concluded that the war was lost and that a government able to negotiate had to exist before the Allies arrived. The German resistance had been trying to kill Hitler since 1938 and had failed or been overtaken every time; what changed in 1944 was Stalingrad behind them, Normandy in front, and the closing of the window in which anything could still be traded. The claim is about the moment and the urgency the war supplied, not about the motives of the conspirators, which were various and partly older than the war.
explanations.world-war-ii--austrian-state-treaty--pre: The English article says that in the immediate aftermath of the war the Allied occupation of Austria began on 27 April 1945, that Austria was divided into four zones jointly occupied by the United Kingdom, the Soviet Union, the United States and France, and that the treaty of 15 May 1955 was signed among those occupying powers and the Austrian government and established Austria as a sovereign state. The treaty ends the occupation the war produced; what it settled about neutrality is its own.
explanations.world-war-ii--azores-agreement-1943--pre: The islands were wanted for one reason and at one moment: the mid-Atlantic gap that land-based aircraft could not cover was where the U-boats were sinking convoys, and by 1943 closing it had become the decisive problem of the Battle of the Atlantic. The alliance of 1373 supplied the form of the request rather than its content — Salazar could concede to an ally what he could not have conceded to a belligerent without abandoning neutrality — and Britain used it precisely because it let a neutral say yes. Telo and Rosas both read the agreement as the point where Portuguese neutrality became a way of joining the winning side without saying so.
explanations.world-war-ii--breakup-of-yugoslavia--pre: The English article on the breakup lists, among the elements that fostered the discord, the formation of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, its first breakup, and the subsequent inter-ethnic and political wars and genocide during the Second World War, beside the ideas of a Greater Albania, a Greater Croatia and a Greater Serbia and the unilateral recognition of the breakaway republics by a newly reunited Germany. One element among several, named by the article, and so a precondition at probable.
explanations.world-war-ii--convention-relating-to-the: The convention of 28 July 1951 was written for the displaced of that war and said so: as adopted it applied only to people who had become refugees as a result of events occurring before 1 January 1951, and the geographical reservation let a state limit it to Europe. The definition, the prohibition on refoulement and the machinery of status all come out of the eight or nine million people the war had left where they did not belong. The claim is about the origin of the instrument; the protocol of 1967 that removed the dateline is not in this atlas and is what turned it into a general one.
explanations.world-war-ii--deportation-of-the-crimean: The English article says the Soviet government presented the deportation as collective punishment, on its claim that some Crimean Tatars collaborated with Nazi Germany in the war — noting that the 20,000 who collaborated with the Axis were half the 40,000 who served in the Red Army — and that several modern scholars instead believe the deportation was part of a plan to gain access to the Dardanelles and acquire territory in Turkey, or to clear minorities from the border regions. The war is the occasion the government gave; the article is explicit that scholars dispute that it is the reason.
explanations.world-war-ii--greco-italian-war--precond: The English article derives the Italian move on Greece from Italy's belligerency: Italy declared war on France and the United Kingdom on 10 June 1940 and by September had invaded France, British Somaliland and Egypt; this "was followed by a hostile press campaign in Italy against Greece, accused of being a British ally", and the provocations culminated in the sinking of the Greek cruiser Elli and Mussolini's ultimatum of 28 October. The article also says the conflict "began the Balkans campaign of World War II", which is why the record is filed under the war as well.
explanations.world-war-ii--indonesian-national-revolu: The English article says the unconditional surrender of Japan on 15 August 1945 was eagerly received by the radical and politicised pemuda groups, who pressured Sukarno and Hatta to proclaim Indonesian independence two days later, on 17 August; the Preparatory Committee elected Sukarno president the following day. The article hangs that on Ricklefs 1991, page 213, among others, which is the second author here. The four-year war that followed was against the Dutch, and the article says the Netherlands was critically weakened by the war in Europe and did not return as a significant military force until early 1946.
explanations.world-war-ii--partition-of-india--precon: The English article says the exchequer of the Attlee government sworn in after the 1945 election had been exhausted by the Second World War and that the British public did not appear enthusiastic about costly distant involvements; late in 1945 the government decided to end the British Raj, and in early 1947 announced its intention to transfer power no later than June 1948. The article hangs that sentence on Metcalf and Metcalf 2006, page 212 — though victorious in war, Britain had suffered immensely and simply did not possess the manpower or economic resources required to coerce a restive India — which is the second author here.
explanations.world-war-ii--treaty-of-san-francisco--c: This is the peace that ended the war’s Pacific half, six years late and on terms the intervening years had changed. Signed by forty-nine states on 8 September 1951, it ended the occupation, took no reparations worth the name, left the territorial questions of the Kuriles and of Taiwan unsettled, and was signed the same day as the security treaty that made Japan an American base. Neither China was a party. The claim is the plain one that the treaty is the settlement of the war; what it argues is that the settlement was made under conditions the war had not produced and the Cold War had.
explanations.world-war-ii--tripartite-pact--caused: The pact is made of the first year of the war. The fall of France in June 1940 left the French and Dutch possessions in Asia without a defender and made the southern advance thinkable; Germany wanted Japan to hold American attention in the Pacific while Britain was dealt with; Italy wanted to be in whatever was signed. None of the three alignments existed in 1938 and all of them are consequences of the campaigns of 1939 and 1940. The claim is about the timing and the terms, not about the ideological affinity, which was older.
explanations.world-war-ii--winter-war--enabled: Finland fought alone because the war had already begun elsewhere. The sympathy of Britain and France was large and their expeditionary plan came to nothing, partly because it depended on crossing Norway and Sweden and partly because both were fighting Germany and would not add the Soviet Union to the list; the League expelled Moscow and could do nothing else. This edge and the one from the Molotov-Ribbentrop pact say different things: the pact is why the Soviet Union could move, the war is why nobody came.
explanations.yom-kippur-war--imf-agreement-1978--prec: Portugal imported all of its oil, and the quadrupling of the price after October 1973 turned a current account that had been in surplus on emigrant remittances into a deficit that grew for four years. The revolution and decolonisation then removed the other supports at once — remittances fell as the European economies closed to migrant labour, the colonial trade ended, and half a million retornados arrived — so the crisis the Fund was called to in 1978 has more than one author. The claim here is that the oil shock is the first of them and the one that came from outside; the argument that the revolution's own economic policy did the rest is made on the Portuguese records.
explanations.young-turk-revolution-of-1908--armenian-: The deportations and killings of 1915 were ordered by the Committee of Union and Progress, which is the organisation that made the revolution of 1908 and which held the Ottoman state after the coup of 1913. The claim is about who was in a position to order it and with what apparatus, not that the constitutional revolution contained the genocide: the Armenian deputies elected in 1908 sat in the parliament the revolution restored, and the programme the Committee carried out in 1915 was one it arrived at after the loss of the Balkans, not one it began with.
explanations.young-turk-revolution-of-1908--bulgarian: The English article says a unilateral declaration would normally have violated the Treaty of Berlin and been unlikely to be approved by the Great Powers, but that **"the chaos that ensued in the Ottoman Empire following the Young Turk Revolution of 1908 provided suitable conditions for the Bulgarian proclamation of independence"** — and that the Powers had turned to their own territorial gains instead, Austria-Hungary to Bosnia, Britain to the Arab provinces, Russia to the Straits. The revolution made the declaration possible; it did not call for it.
explanations.yugoslav-wars--breakup-of-yugoslavia--pr: The English article on the wars says the conflicts both led up to and resulted from the breakup of Yugoslavia, which began in mid-1991, into six independent countries, and that the breakup and the wars are commonly attributed to increasing nationalism and unresolved ethnic tensions. Only the half of that sentence running this way can be drawn: the atlas’s record of the breakup carries Wikidata’s point date of 27 April 1992, the proclamation of the Federal Republic, so an edge the other way would fail the arrow of time against wars the same article dates from 1991. The record needs a person’s reading of its dates before the second half can be written.
explanations.yugoslav-wars--croatian-war-of-independe: The same sentence names the neighbouring parts of Croatia among the places the series of wars primarily affected. The record’s dates are the 1991–1995 its own summary carries, which M44c restored after the import gave it two days that were neither the war’s beginning nor its end; whoever reviews it supplies precise dates from a source they have opened, or leaves the years.
explanations.yugoslav-wars--kosovo-war--precondition-: The article on the breakup says the series of inter-ethnic wars affected Kosovo some years after Bosnia and Croatia. "Some years later" is the article’s own phrase for the distance between them, and is why the campaign of 1999 is drawn as following the series rather than as caused by any one part of it.
